title: NEW [WP-00]: Make `registries/lifts.toml` and the lift headers true — five "lifts" are original code, rand's source row names the wrong file, five guard tests do not exist, every header misstates frankensim's licence; extend `xtask check-lifts` to verify all of it
description:
## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- plan-deps: none (not a plan bead; plan rows BD-007 "lift registry" and BD-037/BD-022 cover creating lifts, not correcting false ones)   proposed-deps: none hard. Coordinate with NEW-evidence-lattice-plan-types (which performs a REAL lift of fs-evidence `color.rs`) and with reopened BD-022 (per-module known answers for eproc/voi/risk/tropical). BD-326 records the owner's RISK-17 licence decision; this bead only states the licence accurately.
- blocks: re-close of BD-007 (lift registry), BD-022, BD-037

Type and priority rationale: priority: 1 (false provenance and a misstated licence grant in a now-public repository; RISK-17 licence question cannot even be posed correctly while headers name the wrong licence)

## Background and why it matters
§27.1 (plan line 6218) sets the header contract for every lifted file: `//! Provenance: frankensim <path> @ <commit>; licence <id>; Changes: <list>; Left out: <list>`. `registries/lifts.toml` holds `{source, commit, sha256_at_lift, target, guard_test}` per file, and "`xtask check-lifts` fails CI on any mismatch between header and registry".

Round 7 found three problems:
- five of eight guard tests do not exist (R7-C096);
- the headers misstate the licence (R7-C164);
- lattice.rs contains none of fs-evidence's identifiers (R7-C082).

This pass measured all eight lifts and found the problem is wider than the guard tests: **five of the eight "lifted" files are not lifts**.

## Goal
Every row in `lifts.toml` describes a file that really derives from the named upstream file at the named commit, with:
- a correct licence id;
- a `Changes` and a `Left out` field;
- a guard test that exists and passes.

Code that was written fresh carries no provenance header. `check-lifts` enforces all of this.

## Current state (FACT)
**Overlap test** (this pass). For each pair, count the distinct, whitespace-trimmed lines longer than 25 characters that occur in both the target and the declared upstream source at `20463525d` (script under References):

| Target | Declared source | Target lines | Shared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fmine-core/src/det.rs` | fs-math/src/det.rs | 152 | 82 (54%) |
| `fmine-core/src/hash.rs` | fs-blake3/src/lib.rs | 174 | 84 (48%) |
| `fmine-core/src/rand.rs` | fs-rand/src/**lib.rs** | 92 | 2 (2%); **20 shared with `fs-rand/src/philox.rs`** |
| `fmine-evidence/src/lattice.rs` | fs-evidence/src/lib.rs | 64 | 0 |
| `fmine-numerics/src/eproc.rs` | fs-eproc/src/lib.rs | 45 | 1 (`pub struct BettingEProcess {`) |
| `fmine-numerics/src/voi.rs` | fs-voi/src/lib.rs | 65 | 2 (`#[derive…]` lines) |
| `fmine-numerics/src/risk.rs` | fs-robust/src/lib.rs | 46 | 2 |
| `fmine-numerics/src/tropical.rs` | fs-tropical/src/lib.rs | 40 | 2 |

- Searching *every* `.rs` file of each declared upstream crate finds at most 2 shared lines for each of the last five. INFERENCE (strong): they were written fresh and given lift headers.
- **Upstream content.** Upstream does have the concepts: fs-eproc has `BettingEProcess`, fs-robust/lib.rs has 22 `cvar` matches, and fs-tropical has `max_plus` only in `tests/tropical.rs`. fs-voi has no `evsi` anywhere, so the guard name `test_normal_evsi_closed_form` points at a capability upstream does not have.
- **rand.** The rand row's `sha256_at_lift` matches `fs-rand/src/lib.rs` at the commit, but the code came from `philox.rs`. The row hashes the wrong file.
- **Guard tests.** These five do not exist: `lattice::tests::test_compose_never_promotes`, `eproc::tests::test_betting_eprocess_ville_bound`, `voi::tests::test_normal_evsi_closed_form`, `risk::tests::test_cvar_rockafellar_uryasev`, `tropical::tests::test_max_plus_critical_cycle`. The files contain `test_lattice_laws_commutative_associative_idempotent`, `test_ville_inequality_type1_error_bound`, `test_evpi_non_negative_and_evsi_monotone`, `test_cvar_coherent_subadditivity_and_monotonicity` and `test_min_plus_longest_path_duality` (R7-C096).
- **Licence.** frankensim's `LICENSE` at `20463525d` reads "MIT License (with OpenAI/Anthropic Rider)", and its `Cargo.toml:185` says `license-file = "LICENSE"`.
  - det.rs, hash.rs and rand.rs say "licence MIT", following `lifts.toml:3`. That omits the rider.
  - The other five say "license: MIT/Apache-2.0", claiming an Apache grant that frankensim does not give. They also lack `Changes:` and `Left out:` (R7-C164).
- **The checker.** `xtask check_lifts` (`crates/xtask/src/lib.rs:424-485`) checks only that line 1 starts with `//! Provenance: frankensim {source} @ {commit};`, and silently skips a missing target (:440-443). It never reads `sha256_at_lift` or `guard_test`, the licence, or the Changes and Left out fields.

## Scope
**In:**
- correcting the eight rows and headers;
- the `check-lifts` extension;
- AGENTS.md/plan wording for the licence id.

**Out:**
- doing the real lifts for eproc, voi, risk and tropical. That is a per-module decision under reopened BD-022.
- the fs-evidence `color.rs` lift (NEW-evidence-lattice-plan-types).
- deciding whether the rider is acceptable (RISK-17, owner and counsel).

## Design
1. **Original code loses its lift claim.**
   - For lattice, eproc, voi, risk and tropical, replace the provenance header with `//! Original FrankenMining code (not lifted). Upstream analogue: frankensim <path> @ 20463525d (not copied).` Remove their five `[[lift]]` rows. This edits the registry; no file is deleted (RULE 1).
   - Add a `[[analogue]]` table with `{target, upstream, note}`, so GATE-FSIM-DRIFT still knows which upstream regions are relevant.
   - If the owner prefers real lifts, each becomes a BD-022 subtask instead. Until then, the record must not say "lifted".
2. **rand.** The row becomes `source = "crates/fs-rand/src/philox.rs"` with that file's sha256 at `20463525d`, computed by the implementer. The header gets the same correction.
3. **Licence id.** Every remaining lift header and `lifts.toml:3` say `licence LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider`. That is asupersync's SPDX-style id for the same text, which keeps it consistent with BD-326. The workspace's own `license = "MIT"` mismatch is BD-326's; do not fix it twice.
4. **`check-lifts` v2** (about 80 changed lines):
   - (a) a missing target is an error;
   - (b) the header has all four fields: path, commit, `licence <id>` with the id equal to the registry's new `licence` column, and non-empty `Changes:` and `Left out:`;
   - (c) `guard_test` exists: `fn <name>(` inside the target file's `#[cfg(test)]` module;
   - (d) the `sha256_at_lift` format is 64 hex characters;
   - (e) `xtask check-lifts --upstream <path>` (local only, not CI, since CI has no frankensim checkout) recomputes the sha256 from `git show <commit>:<source>` and reports the overlap ratio. A lifted file under 20% overlap is flagged as "not a lift" (DESIGN threshold; det, hash and rand-vs-philox sit at about 22–54%).
   - (f) any file carrying `//! Provenance: frankensim` must have a row.
5. **Guard tests for the three real lifts** already exist and pass in CI run 40974504857.

**Worked example.**
- **Today:** `check-lifts` v2 reports 5 missing guard tests, 8 licence-id mismatches, 5 missing Changes/Left out fields, and, with `--upstream`, 5 files under 20% overlap plus the rand sha256 computed against the wrong file.
- **After the fix:** 3 rows (det, hash, rand→philox) and 0 errors.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `lifts.toml` has rows only for det, hash and rand. Each header has all four fields and `licence LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider`.
2. `rg -n "MIT/Apache-2.0" crates/` returns nothing. `rg -n "Provenance: frankensim" crates/` equals the row set.
3. A seeded fixture missing a guard test, missing `Left out:`, or with a wrong licence id fails `check-lifts`. A missing target fails.
4. The local `--upstream` run output is quoted in the close reason, showing the rand sha256 equals `philox.rs` at `20463525d`.

## Tests
- **Unit, on string fixtures, one per rule (a)–(f):** positive and negative.
- **Known answer:** the overlap ratio for det.rs against fs-math/src/det.rs ≥ 0.5, as a local-only test gated on the `FRANKENSIM_PATH` environment variable.
- **Mutation:** delete `test_golden_hash_10k_inputs`'s name from det.rs; `check-lifts` must fail.

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **Removing lift claims loses the upstream link.** The `[[analogue]]` table keeps it.
- **The overlap heuristic is crude.** Use it only as a local flag, never as CI pass/fail. The definitive evidence is the header plus a reviewer diff.
- **Never** claim a licence grant upstream does not give, and never claim code was lifted when it was not.

## Subtasks
Not needed (one commit for the registry and headers, one for the checker).

## References
- Plan §27.1 (6187–6230), lift order (6205–6212), RISK-17, BD-007, BD-022 and BD-037 rows.
- R7-C082, R7-C096, R7-C164. K.2 finding 7.
- Files: `registries/lifts.toml`, `crates/xtask/src/lib.rs:424-485`, the eight target files, frankensim `LICENSE` and `Cargo.toml@20463525d`.
- Script: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jemanuel-projects-franken-mining/2ba72fbb-c45d-4fd8-93cf-c08cb26d7a18/scratchpad/lift_overlap.py`.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Check out frankensim at `20463525d` next to this repository.
2. For each row of `registries/lifts.toml`, count distinct whitespace-trimmed lines longer than 25 characters shared by the target file and its declared upstream file. Expected today: det.rs 82 (54%), hash.rs 84 (48%), rand.rs 2 against `fs-rand/src/lib.rs` but 20 against `philox.rs`, and 0-2 for lattice.rs, eproc.rs, voi.rs, risk.rs and tropical.rs.
3. `rg -n "fn test_compose_never_promotes|fn test_betting_eprocess_ville_bound|fn test_normal_evsi_closed_form|fn test_cvar_rockafellar_uryasev|fn test_max_plus_critical_cycle" crates/` returns nothing, although the lift headers name these guard tests.
4. `head -3` of each lifted file: three say "licence MIT", five say "MIT/Apache-2.0"; frankensim's LICENSE reads "MIT License (with OpenAI/Anthropic Rider)".
5. `cargo run -p xtask -- check-all` passes anyway: `check_lifts` (`crates/xtask/src/lib.rs:424-485`) reads only line 1 and skips a missing target.

## E2E test script and logging
- **E2E.** `cargo xtask check-all` includes `check-lifts`. The mutation control (deleting `test_golden_hash_10k_inputs`'s name) is run once in a scratch checkout, and its failing output is quoted in the close reason.
- **Logging.** `check-lifts` prints one line per `[[lift]]` row: path, upstream, commit, rule results (a) to (f), overlap ratio when `FRANKENSIM_PATH` is set. One line per header that has no registry row.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `lifts.toml` has rows only for det, hash and rand. Each header has all four fields and `licence LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider`.
2. `rg -n "MIT/Apache-2.0" crates/` returns nothing. `rg -n "Provenance: frankensim" crates/` equals the row set.
3. A seeded fixture missing a guard test, missing `Left out:`, or with a wrong licence id fails `check-lifts`. A missing target fails.
4. The local `--upstream` run output is quoted in the close reason, showing the rand sha256 equals `philox.rs` at `20463525d`.
close_reason: commit:fe10aa5; record:planning/mor/MOR_CASE.md E852. C1: lifts.toml has rows for det, hash and rand only, plus 5 analogues; each header has all four fields and licence LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider. C2: MIT/Apache-2.0 appears 0 times in crates/; header lines equal the row set (the only other hit is the checker's own constant in xtask/src/lifts.rs). C3: test:xtask::lifts::tests::test_rule_a_missing_target_fails, test_rule_b_header_fields, test_rule_c_guard_test_must_be_in_the_test_module, test_rule_d_forms_and_licence, test_rule_f_provenance_needs_a_row_and_analogues_say_original; mutation: renaming test_golden_hash_10k_inputs fails check-lifts. C4: check-lifts --upstream /Users/jemanuel/projects/frankensim at 20463525d gives rand.rs vs crates/fs-rand/src/philox.rs sha256 2cb5bbfe21d6bf54... sha_ok true, 20 of 92 shared. Deviation: the bead's det.rs >= 0.5 known answer no longer holds (file grew, 82 of 198), so the test pins the shared count of 82. Limit: CI rules cannot detect a self-consistent wrong source; only the local --upstream run can. Self-verified in a fresh re-execution at HEAD; not independently verified; nothing has run in CI.

title: BD-347 [WP-03]: Reliance status for issued outputs and reviewed decisions: issuance record (digest, output Claims, anchor), withdrawal and supersession events, an outbound register of issued copies by recipient role, consumer check current / withdrawn / superseded / unknown
description:
_Plan row BD-347 (WP-03). Scope in one line: Reliance status for issued outputs — issuance records, withdrawal and supersession events, an outbound register by recipient role, and a consumer check that refuses current reuse of a withdrawn output_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-329
- plan-deps: BD-329
- proposed-deps: BD-329, unchanged. BD-329 supplies the digest, the anchor and the per-number citations that an issuance record points to.
- blocks: none

Type and priority rationale: priority: 2 (M1; the failure class it addresses is the one round 7 found)

## Background and why it matters
Codex and Claude proposed this independently, as blind spots that none of the duel's 45 ideas covered.
- **Codex (BS-COD-01, self-score 810).** A holder of a detached report needs to learn that its producer has withdrawn it.
- **Claude (B3, self-score 590).** Track which copies left the system, and recall them by Claim or by code revision.
- **Codex's COD-04** ("recall decisions when their evidence changes") was narrowed and merged in.

**What round 7 showed.** It found the defect class concretely. Every figure the original M0 slice emitted came from an in-code stand-in labelled as Barrick's (K.2 finding 1). That defect was in the code, not the evidence: the source files never changed, so no staleness mechanism would ever fire.

**The gap.** INV-013 marks a Claim stale only when it is read again. A board pack, an emailed figure or an agent's memory note is never read again.

**The test (K.5).** A withdrawn output is refused for current reuse, while its historical digest still verifies.

## Goal
Every output that leaves through a FrankenMining export path writes an issuance record. A later withdrawal or supersession is an append-only event.
- `fmine reliance check <file|digest> [--as-of t]` answers one of: `current`, `withdrawn`, `superseded` or `unknown`.
- The export and report path refuses to present a withdrawn output's numbers as current. Historical inspection still opens the original bytes and shows their historical status.
- `fmine recall --revision <rev>` and `fmine recall --claim <id>` list every issued output a defective revision produced, or that cites a superseded Claim.

## Current state
- **None of this exists.** Today's `fmine assure public` emits a report with its INV-002 flags, its certificates, its `next_actions` and a blake3 state root, but nothing records that the report was issued or to whom (FACT: `crates/fmine-public/src/lib.rs`, `to_json` and `assess`).
- **Staleness exists only inside the graph.** `ClaimDag::invalidate_and_propagate` (`crates/fmine-claim/src/lib.rs:395`) marks dependent Claims stale for readers that are still inside it.

## Scope
**In:**
- issuance records;
- withdrawal and supersession events;
- the consumer check;
- recall by revision and by Claim;
- the export-path gate;
- an outbound register keyed by recipient role;
- a synthetic first slice.

**Out:**
- automatic notifications or emails;
- signed status receipts distributed to partners (later, through admitted trust mechanisms);
- personal data of any kind.

## Design
**`IssuanceRecord`**
- Fields: `{output_digest (blake3 of the exact bytes), output_claims: sorted Claim ids, anchor (state root), code_revision, binary_digest, input_manifest_root, lane and taint, issued_at, recipient_role (a generic role id such as "sponsor", "reviewer-pool-1" or "agent-session:<id>"), purpose}`.
- No names, emails or contact details.

**`StatusEvent`** is one of:
- `Withdrawn{output_digest, reason, affected_claims, defect_class: CodeDefect | SourceRestated | ScopeError, by_role, at}`;
- `Superseded{output_digest, by_digest, at}`.

A withdrawal names the affected statements, never "everything", unless every statement is affected. It names a replacement only when one exists. A replacement can itself be withdrawn later.

**Storage.** An append-only, hash-chained file in the workspace state directory: each line carries the blake3 of the previous line. It is product state, because the export path branches on it.
- This is the smallest seam until the authority ledger exists (BD-090, FMT-CAS-1). It moves there unchanged when that lands.
- No parallel registry is kept once it does.

**Consumer check.** `check(digest, as_of, status_cut)` returns:
- `current`, when there is no event up to the cut and the cut is fresh under the owner's freshness policy;
- `withdrawn{reason, affected, replacement?}`;
- `superseded{by}`;
- `unknown`, when the digest was never issued here, the status cut is stale, or the trusted time is unavailable.

**Gate.** A request for current reuse of a withdrawn output is a typed refusal in the 2xx evidence family, exit 3 (§30.1). The new code is to be registered through BD-328, for example "issued output withdrawn or superseded".
- The refusal names the replacement, or tells the caller to request status.
- Agents can prepare a withdrawal (§30.4); a human role releases it.

**Recall.**
- `recall --revision r` returns every issuance record whose `code_revision` is r.
- `recall --claim c` returns every record whose `output_claims` contain c, or whose Claim is superseded.

**Known-answer shape.** Reproduce round 7's defect synthetically:
- three code revisions, each producing N outputs on a synthetic issuer, held by two generic roles;
- revision 2 substitutes a generated input and is declared defective;
- no source file changes.

Never fabricate figures labelled as an issuer's to build this test.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. After withdrawal, the old output's digest still verifies against its bytes and anchor, but a current-use check refuses with the registered code.
2. **Recall is exact (property test).** Over random revisions, outputs and supersessions, `recall` returns exactly the outputs whose revision is defective or whose Claims include a superseded one.
3. **`unknown` is never `current`.** An unseen digest, an expired status cut or missing trusted time all give `unknown`.
4. **No personal data.** The recipient field accepts role ids only (schema test).

## Tests
- **Protocol cases:**
  - an offline reader;
  - a replayed stale status;
  - a replacement that is itself withdrawn;
  - one defect affecting several issued copies with no source change;
  - an unauthorised withdrawal attempt.
- **Hash-chain tamper test.** Editing any line breaks verification. That is a FMINE-REF-502 class integrity refusal.
- **Agent lease task (GATE-ROBOT-01).** An agent caches an answer, the Claim is then superseded, and the agent must revalidate before reuse.

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **Kill (K.5):** holders never reuse detached outputs. Keep only the export-path check.
- **Kill (B3):** fewer than 50% of figures in a sampled board pack carry a resolvable Claim token after one quarter (measured with BD-345). Drop the recipient half and keep recall by revision.
- **Risk:** the register becomes ceremony that gates nothing. Then retire it; the gate is the product.
- **Never:**
  - claim that all copies were recalled; report only the issued population known;
  - carry an old sign-off forward;
  - store personal data.

## References
- Plan: §30.1, §30.4–30.5 (lines 6730–6850); INV-013; §37.3 M1 (line 7661); K.5 row 9 (line 9397); bead row at line 8017.
- Duel: Codex BS-COD-01 (`planning/duel/WIZARD_BLINDSPOTS_COD.md`); Claude B3 (`WIZARD_BLINDSPOTS_CC.md`); COD-04 (`WIZARD_IDEAS_COD.md` §4).
- Code: `crates/fmine-public/src/lib.rs`, `crates/fmine-claim/src/lib.rs`.

## E2E test script and logging
- **E2E.** The verbs `fmine reliance check <file or digest> [--as-of t]`, `fmine recall --revision <rev>` and `fmine recall --claim <id>` run in `scripts/e2e/reliance.sh` over one protocol:
  1. issue a report from `fmine assure public --synthetic`;
  2. record the issuance;
  3. supersede one Claim;
  4. query status as an offline reader with a stale status file;
  5. withdraw;
  6. replace;
  7. withdraw the replacement;
  8. attempt an unauthorised withdrawal.
  The `reliance check` answer at each step (`current`, `superseded`, `withdrawn` or `unknown`) is golden. `recall` lists exactly the issued copies that cite the superseded Claim. A tampered status-chain line is refused (FMINE-REF-502 class). The same sequence also runs as a library-level Rust test, so `cargo test` covers it.
- **Logging.** One line per protocol step: issuance id, output digest, status, the chain head after the step, and any refusal code.

## Background and why it matters
Round 7 added five owner questions to plan §36.2 (lines ~7482–7486). Three had the deadline "before the next push" or "before the next code push":
- **OPEN-R7-1** (Owner + counsel): may derived Barrick workbook values be committed to the public repository? (RISK-31). Default: "Locators, URLs, sha256 and computed results only".
- **OPEN-R7-4** (Owner): should the public plan keep the Avathon governance passage (§31, §35 F1, §34.4)? (R7-C030, R7-C032). Default: "Keep the factual, sourced statement; drop characterisations".
- **OPEN-R7-5** (Owner): what happens to the unpushed M0 commit `68e7091` (amend, follow with a fix commit, or push as is)? Default: "Do not push until R001–R002 of Appendix K.2 are done".

FACT: on 2026-10-29 the owner asked for all changes to be committed and pushed. `origin/main` and `origin/master` are at `748da79`; the repository is PUBLIC (`gh repo view`). `68e7091` is in public history, followed by the correcting commits `543df53` (real-file lane and five-state ledger), `d5ffced`, `d6e2678` and `748da79`. K.2 step 2 (BD-323, correcting the bead and INT records) was not done before the push.

The plan therefore states as open, with a past deadline, decisions that the push either made or overtook. A future reader cannot tell what was decided.

K.2 step 2 (BD-323) was not complete at the push; its correction is tracked as BD-323." Update the K.2 sentence "Whether to amend `68e7091` … is the owner's decision (OPEN-R7-5)" the same way. History is never rewritten (AGENTS: no force push, no `git reset --hard`).
- **OPEN-R7-1: still the owner's and counsel's.** The push carried MOR_CASE entries that quote individual workbook values (for example E820–E823 cite cell values such as Kibali Q2 2024 TCC 70 against 72). Record that fact, keep the default (locators, URLs, sha256, computed results) as the rule for new commits, and set a new deadline: before the next push that adds derived values. List the files that already quote values so the owner can decide on them in one pass.
- **OPEN-R7-4: still the owner's.** Record that the passages were pushed unchanged, and set the deadline "before the next push".
- **Do not decide for the owner.** This bead records facts and asks; it never edits those passages or removes quoted values on its own.

title: NEW [WP-03]: Remove silent clamps: `solve_cutoff_grade` clamps recovery, floors the price and returns an unconverged iterate; `winkler_interval_score` clamps alpha
description:
## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- plan-deps: none (found 2026-10-29 while expanding BD-350.S3 and BD-341)   proposed-deps: none
- blocks: BD-350 S3 (resource checks reuse the cut-off solver)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 2 (both are reachable from public-lane code paths and contradict "refuse, never clamp"; `winkler_interval_score` runs inside `evaluate_model`; the cut-off solver is the code behind closed bd-275's E182–E184 claim)

## Background and why it matters
AGENTS.md rule 5: "Refuse, never clamp or plug." A clamp turns an input outside its domain into a different, plausible-looking number, so a wrong input produces a confident wrong answer instead of a refusal. The same rule motivated the IRR bead (`brent_root` returns a non-root after `max_iter`).

FACT (HEAD 748da79):
- `crates/fmine-metrics/src/lib.rs:176-197` `solve_cutoff_grade(processing_and_ga_usd_per_t, net_metal_price_usd_per_unit, initial_guess, recovery_fn) -> (f64, usize)`:
  - line 185: `initial_guess.max(1e-6)`;
  - line 186: `net_metal_price_usd_per_unit.max(1e-9)` (a zero or negative price becomes 1e-9);
  - line 188: `recovery_fn(g).clamp(0.05, 0.999)` (a recovery of 0 or 1.2 becomes 0.05 or 0.999);
  - line 196: after 100 damped iterations without meeting `1e-10`, it returns `(g, 100)` as if solved.
  The module header claims it reproduces E182–E184 for BD-275; its only test (`lib.rs:270`) does not check E182.
- `crates/fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:227` `winkler_interval_score`: `alpha.clamp(1e-6, 1.0 - 1e-6)`; line 228 `(hi - lo).max(0.0)` turns an inverted interval into width 0. It is called by `evaluate_model` (`lib.rs:125`) with alpha 0.20.

## Goal
Both functions refuse out-of-domain inputs and non-convergence with typed errors; callers map them to refusals; known answers stay green.

## Design (DESIGN)
- `solve_cutoff_grade` returns `Result<CutoffSolution { grade, iterations, residual }, CutoffError>` with `NonPositivePrice`, `RecoveryOutOfDomain { at_grade, value }` (outside (0, 1]), `NotConverged { iterations, last_step }`, `NonFinite`. No floors, no clamps.
- `winkler_interval_score` returns `Result<f64, ScoreError>` with `AlphaOutOfDomain` (alpha not in (0, 1)) and `InvertedInterval { lo, hi }`.
- Callers: `evaluate_model` propagates the error as a refusal of that record's score, never as a skipped record (the denominator rule of BD-343 applies).
- Determinism: no new transcendentals (NEW-det-portable-kernels).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Price 0, recovery 1.2, recovery 0, and a recovery function that oscillates for 100 iterations each return their typed error (today they return a number).
2. alpha = 0 or 1, and lo > hi, each return a typed error.
3. The existing cut-off known answer still converges; E182 is added as a known answer with its cited inputs, or the module header's E182–E184 claim is removed until it is (BD-323 decides bd-275's status).
4. `rg -n "\.clamp\(|\.max\(1e-|\.min\(1\.0 -" crates/fmine-metrics/src crates/fmine-calib/src` lists no remaining clamp in a scoring or solving path without a comment stating why it is not a domain clamp.

## Tests
Unit tests per error variant; property test: for random valid inputs the solved grade satisfies the fixed-point equation within tolerance, and for random invalid inputs no `Ok` is returned; regression tests pinned to the 2026-10-29 findings.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In a unit test call `solve_cutoff_grade(14.5, 0.0, 0.0025, |_| 0.9)`: today it returns a grade (price floored to 1e-9) instead of refusing.
2. Call it with `|_| 1.2` as the recovery function: the recovery is silently clamped to 0.999.
3. Call `winkler_interval_score(1.0, 3.0, 0.0, 2.0)`: alpha 0 is clamped to 1e-6 and a score is returned.

## References
`crates/fmine-metrics/src/lib.rs:6, 176-197, 270`; `crates/fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:125, 227-228`; AGENTS.md rule 5; bd-275; BD-350 dossier.

## E2E test script and logging
- **E2E.** `evaluate_model` (the only production caller of `winkler_interval_score`, `fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:125`) gets a test in which one record has an inverted interval. The model's score for that record is refused, and the cohort denominator is unchanged. No verb calls `solve_cutoff_grade` today; BD-350.S3's verb test carries its e2e.
- **Logging.** The property tests log the seed, inputs and the returned variant for any failure.

title: BD-332 [WP-03]: Vintage and basis key on public Claims (subject, valid period, reporting vintage, ownership basis, scope, unit) with the raw token; numeric zero in a disposed or withheld column stays `Nil`
description:
_Plan row BD-332 (WP-03). Scope in one line: Vintage and basis key on public Claims, with the raw token kept_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-059, BD-322
- plan-deps: BD-059, BD-322   proposed-deps: BD-322 and NEW-cell-number-formats. BD-059 is closed under the generic reason; its builder exists but is used only in a test. Add a label-anchored Mine Stats reader, which no bead delivers today: ask BD-323 to reopen BD-271, whose done-when promised one.
- blocks: NEW-gate-bull-01-part3-vintage-consistency, BD-341, BD-345 (plan)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 1 (GATE-BULL-01 part 3 and BD-341, BD-343 and BD-345 cannot compare figures across vintages or bases without this key)

## Background and why it matters
The same figure appears in several workbooks: as first published, and later as a comparative, sometimes restated. Two observed cases (FACT):
- Barrick's Total Gold 2024Q1 AISC was first published as 1,479 (`Q1_2024:QTD!G23`). It reappears as 1,474 (`Q1_2025:QTD!N22`) with no footnote (E474; W1-DR-08).
- Across the ten Mine Stats files, 9 of 6,391 comparative cells changed without a footnote (W1 T16).

Ownership basis is part of every figure (AGENTS.md). Porgera is labelled 47.5% in the Q2/Q3 2024 summaries but 24.5% on its site sheet, and the values fit 24.5% (W1-DR-01).

Divested sites keep their columns, filled with placeholders and numeric zeros:
- Tongon was sold and closed on 1 Dec 2025. Its recovery is numeric 0 at `Q1_2026:Minestats3!F19`, `Q2_2026:Minestats3!F19` and `F64` (FACT, W1 §10).
- Hemlo's equivalent zeros are at `Q1_2026:Minestats1!N27`/`N28` and the same cells in Q2 2026.

A reader that types those zeros as numbers reports a 0% recovery that never happened. B7 adopted the rule "bind each value to bytes *and* interpretation … with the raw token kept" (K.4 item 1).

## Goal
Every public Claim carries a key with these fields:
- subject;
- valid period;
- reporting vintage;
- ownership basis;
- scope;
- unit;
- line;
- the raw token.

With that key:
- first publications and restated comparatives coexist as distinct Claims in one series;
- a numeric zero in a disposed or withheld column is `Nil` with its token kept, never a value.

## Current state
FACT, HEAD 748da79.
- **No key fields on Claims.** `Claim<T>` (`crates/fmine-claim/src/lib.rs:106-122`) has `metric_key`, `representation`, evidence, knowledge, anchors (path, sha256, locator), `supersedes`, `stale`, and nothing else. There is no subject, period, vintage, basis, scope or unit.
- **The builder is unused and types zeros as exact values.** `cell_to_public_claim` (`crates/fmine-public/src/lib.rs:34-86`) is called only in a test (R7-C062). It labels every numeric cell `Exact`/`KnownKnown`, including a numeric zero in a disposed column. It types every placeholder token as one undifferentiated `Placeholder(token)`.
- **The reader has one placeholder bucket.** `fmine-io` maps `-`, `–`, `—`, `N/A`, `n/a`, `NA`, `na` to `CellValue::Placeholder` (`crates/fmine-io/src/xlsx.rs:439-461`). Appendix I asks for four types:
  - `—` → `Nil{unknown}`;
  - `n/a` → `NotApplicable`;
  - blank → `Missing`;
  - a numeric-zero placeholder → `Nil` (plan Appendix I.9).
- **Ledger instances carry part of a key.** `IdentityInstance` has file (which implies the vintage), sheet (the period label), subject and family. It has no parsed period, no ownership basis and no unit. The 12 Loulo-Gounkoto 2025 all-zero columns become `NotPublished("all-zero column")` (E822), which is the right outcome, reached by a heuristic.
- **Mine Stats are not interpreted.** The files are loaded, censused and read for E816 label checks, but there is no label-anchored table reader for them (R7-C025 found none, and none was added). The Tongon known answer lives in Mine Stats.

## Scope
**In:**
- the key type;
- value typing;
- the subject-status registry;
- period and ownership parsing;
- Claim construction for AISC-table cells and Mine Stats per-site blocks (the latter once that reader exists);
- series grouping across vintages.

**Out:**
- the consistency verdicts across vintages (NEW-gate-bull-01-part3);
- issuer reserve rows (BD-335);
- the Claim store and `claim show` (WP-02).

## Design
**Key** (DESIGN):

```rust
pub struct PublicKey {
    issuer: String,
    subject: SubjectId,                       // registered subject, footnote letter stripped
    valid_period: Period,                     // {year, kind: Q(1..4) | H1 | NineMonths | FY}
    reporting_vintage: Vintage,               // {release: "2025Q2", file_sha256}
    ownership_basis: OwnershipBasis,          // Consolidated100 | Attributable{pct: Option<Ratio>, source: Printed|Registry} | Unprinted
    scope: Scope,                             // Site | JointVenture | Region{map_version} | Company
    unit: UnitId,                             // registered: usd_m, koz, usd_per_oz, kt, g_per_t, fraction …
    line: LineKey,                            // normalised row label + occurrence index (two NCI rows exist)
}
pub enum PublicValue {
    Number { stored: DecimalText, displayed: Option<DecimalText> },
    Nil { token: String, reason: NilReason }, // Unknown | Withheld | Disposed | NotPublished
    NotApplicable { token: String },
    Missing,
}
```

- **Series key.** `series_key = key − reporting_vintage`. Claims in the same series are the "same figure" across vintages.
- **Claim id.** The id includes the full key and the raw token, so first publication and comparative get distinct ids.
- **Periods.** Parsed from sheet names (`Q2 2024`, `YTD Q2 2025`, `YTD Sept 30 2024`, `2025`, …) and Mine Stats headers ("For the three months ended March 31," plus a year cell). An unparsed period is a table refusal, never a guess.
- **Ownership.** The printed `(x%)` is parsed from Mine Stats headers. It is never defaulted to 100%; where none is printed, the basis is `Unprinted`. A registry override with an evidence id (Porgera 24.5%, W1-DR-01) keeps the printed value beside it.
- **Subject status** (registry data, `registries/sources/barrick.toml`, or a `[[subject_status]]` table if NEW-quarterly-vintage-ingestion lands first):

| subject | status | from | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tongon | disposed | 2025-12-01 | E485–E488, E553, E554 |
| Hemlo | disposed | 2025-11-26 | same |
| Loulo-Gounkoto | withheld | 2025Q1–2025Q3 | E818 |
| Long Canyon | care and maintenance, not reported | 2024Q1 | W1 §10 |

- **Zero rule.** A numeric 0 in a cell whose (subject, valid period) is disposed or withheld becomes `Nil{token:"0", reason}`. Evidence class `Placeholder`, knowledge `KnownUnknown`.
- **Divided columns.** The AISC workbooks' zeros for Loulo-Gounkoto 2025 fall under the same rule (E497). Those zeros display as `-` under the accounting format (`_(* "-"??_)` zero section; E497). NEW-cell-number-formats records the displayed token.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Known answers** (FACT locators):
- `Q1_2026:Minestats3!F19`, `Q2_2026:Minestats3!F19` and `F64` (Tongon recovery) are `Nil{Disposed}`. No Claim has value 0.
- `Q1_2026:Minestats1!N27`/`N28` (Hemlo) are the same.
- `Q1_2024:QTD!G23` = 1,479 and `Q1_2025:QTD!N22` = 1,474 are two Claims with equal `series_key`, distinct ids, and vintages 2024Q1 and 2025Q1.
- Porgera Q2 2024 carries printed 47.5%, registry 24.5% and the evidence W1-DR-01.
- A `—` is `Nil{Unknown}`, an `n/a` is `NotApplicable`, and a blank inside a data block is `Missing`. W1-DR-12's mixed tokens (`Q2_2024:Minestats1!H35` `n/a` against `H95` `—`) keep their tokens.
- Every AISC-table instance of the five-state ledger can return its operands' keys.

## Tests
- Unit tests:
  - the period parser over every sheet name in the eight AISC workbooks;
  - an unknown sheet name is refused;
  - the ownership parser on `Porgera (24.5%)1` and `Site G (60%)1`.
- Property test: Claim ids differ whenever any key field or the raw token differs.
- Synthetic known answers: a synthetic disposed site whose numeric 0 becomes `Nil`.
- Real-file ignored test: the counts of each value type per file, pinned against an independent Python reader written first.
- Negative test: removing Tongon's disposal row from the registry makes the Tongon-zero test fail. That proves the registry is the source of the rule, not code.

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **Disposal dates.**
  - Risk: a disposal date that falls inside a quarter. Tongon closed on 1 Dec 2025, and the Q4 2025 stub has real values.
  - Rule: status applies from the first period entirely after the date. A stub quarter keeps its numbers.
- **A missing Mine Stats reader.**
  - Risk: without it, the Mine Stats half of this bead cannot ship.
  - Fallback: ship the AISC-table half, and list the Mine Stats known answers as blocked by name.
- **This bead must never:** emit 0 as a recovery or production for a disposed site, default ownership to 100%, or overwrite a first publication with a later comparative.

## Subtasks
1. **Key and value types, and the subject-status registry.**
   - Acceptance: the unit and property tests; the registry golden test.
2. **AISC-table Claims with keys.**
   - Acceptance: every instance's operands are keyed. Depends on 1.
3. **Mine Stats per-site Claims.**
   - Acceptance: the Tongon, Hemlo, E474 and W1-DR-01 known answers. Depends on 1 and on the Mine Stats reader.

## References
- Plan §21.6 (import rules, vintages), Appendix I.9 (import rules and token mapping); K.4 item 1.
- E474, E497, E818, E485–E488, E553, E554.
- W1 §6 (DR-01, DR-08, DR-09, DR-12), §10, §13, T16.
- R7-C025, R7-C062.
- `crates/fmine-claim/src/lib.rs`, `crates/fmine-public/src/lib.rs`, `crates/fmine-io/src/xlsx.rs`.

## E2E test script and logging
- **E2E.** The `assure public` e2e (BD-331's script) also asserts that every emitted Claim carries the full key `(subject, valid period, reporting vintage, ownership basis, construction)` and that no two Claims share an id. The synthetic disposed site must show `Nil` with its registry row cited.
- **Logging.** One line per file with counts per value type (`Number`, `Nil`, `NotApplicable`, `Missing`, `Text`). One line per subject-status rule applied (subject, period, rule id, cells affected). The negative test (Tongon's row removed) logs the failing assertion with the cell locator.

title: BD-332.S2 [WP-03]: AISC-table Claims with keys
description:
## Context
Subtask S2 of BD-332: "BD-332 [WP-03]: Vintage and basis key on public Claims (subject, valid period, reporting vintage, ownership basis, scope, unit) with the raw token; numeric zero in a disposed or withheld column stays `Nil`". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** Every public Claim carries a key with these fields:
- subject;
- valid period;
- reporting vintage;
- ownership basis;
- scope;
- unit;
- line;
- the raw token.

With that key:
- first publications and restated comparatives coexist as distinct Claims in one series;
- a numeric zero in a disposed or withheld column is `Nil` with its token kept, never a value.

## Work
Builds on S1, and on BD-329.S1's `operands`. **Files:** `crates/fmine-public/src/aisc.rs` and `lib.rs`.

**1. Key every operand.** Each `Operand` of every `IdentityInstance` gains `key: PublicKey` and `value: PublicValue`.

| Key field | Source |
|---|---|
| subject | `match_subject` on the column header. It strips one footnote letter. FACT: `Barrick_Q1_2025_AISC.xlsx` `'Q1 2025'!N4` reads 'Loulo-Gounkotok' |
| valid period | `parse_sheet_period` on the sheet name |
| vintage | `RegisteredSource.quarter` plus the file's sha256 |
| scope | the subject registry (site or region) |
| unit | `usd_m` for $M rows, `koz` for ounces, `usd_per_oz` for rates |
| line | normalised row label plus occurrence index |

**Ownership basis** comes from a registered row-basis table, one evidence id per row. Two FACT anchors:
- the ounces row reads 'Ounces sold - attributable basis (000s ounces)';
- footnote g says CoS per ounce uses ownership share.

A row without a registered basis is `Unprinted`.

**2. Replace `cell_to_public_claim`** (`lib.rs:34-86`, test-only today, R7-C062) with `public_claim(cell, key, value) -> Claim<PublicValue>`. Every operand can return its Claim.

**3. Withheld zeros.**
- FACT: `Barrick_Q1_2025_AISC.xlsx` `'Q1 2025'` column N holds numeric 0 at N5, N18, N19 and N23.
- With the Loulo-Gounkoto row (withheld 2025Q1–Q3, E818), these become `Nil{token:"0", Withheld}`. They display as `-` (E497).
- The ledger's np reason then cites the status row instead of the "all-zero column" heuristic.
- E822 has 12 all-zero columns. Each one either matches a status row or is listed as `unregistered_all_zero` for the owner, never silently `Nil`. The census decides the split.

**4. Series grouping.** Add `series(&[Claim]) -> BTreeMap<SeriesKey, Vec<Claim>>`, ordered by release.

**Known answers** (FACT, read 2026-10-29):
- **Pueblo Viejo H1 2025 AISC.** Two locations:
  - `Barrick_Q2_2025_AISC.xlsx` `'YTD Q2 2025'!J18` = 272 (J4 'Pueblo Viejo', A18 'All-in sustaining costs');
  - `Barrick_Q2_2026_AISC.xlsx` `'YTD Q2 2025'!I17` = 272 (I4, A17).

  They share one series key, with distinct ids and vintages 2025Q2 and 2026Q2. A column-based match would pair the wrong cells.
- **Kibali `'Q2 2024'!O11` = 70** in `Barrick_Q3_2024_AISC.xlsx` and `Barrick_Q2_2025_AISC.xlsx`: one series.

**Hands over** to NEW-gate-bull-01-part3 S1 (keyed first publications), BD-341 and BD-345.

**Never:**
- overwrite a first publication;
- key by column letter;
- default a row's basis.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Keyed operands.** Every operand of the 2,595 real and 35 synthetic instances carries a key and a typed value, with 0 unparsed periods.
- **Pueblo Viejo.** J18 and I17 share a series key and have distinct claim ids.
- **Kibali.** The two O11 cells share a series key.
- **Withheld zeros.** The four Loulo-Gounkoto zeros in `'Q1 2025'` column N are `Nil{Withheld}`. No Claim has value 0 for a withheld quarter.
- **All-zero columns.** E822's 12 are each matched to a status row or listed as `unregistered_all_zero`.
- **Series counts.** The number of series with two or more vintages equals an independent census. Part 3's scratch read is 2,980 of 5,819 keys (INFERENCE, not in the register); pin only the census.
- **States unchanged.** Ledger states and counts equal E822's.

## Tests and logging
- **Unit:**
  - `test_operand_keys_synthetic_complete`;
  - `test_subject_strips_one_footnote_letter_loulo_gounkotok`;
  - `test_row_without_registered_basis_is_unprinted`;
  - `test_public_claim_replaces_cell_to_public_claim`.
- **Series:**
  - `test_series_grouping_two_vintages_distinct_ids`;
  - `test_column_based_match_would_fail`, a negative control using a synthetic shifted column.
- **Known answers** (ignored; real file):
  - `barrick_pv_h1_2025_j18_i17_same_series`;
  - `barrick_kibali_o11_two_vintages_same_series`;
  - `barrick_lg_q1_2025_zeros_nil_withheld`.
- **Real file:** `barrick_every_operand_keyed_matches_census` (ignored; needs the gitignored corpus; BD-339's CI job).
  - One log line per file: `{file, sha256, operands, numbers, nil, not_applicable, missing, unparsed}`.
  - A summary line: `{operands, series, multi_vintage_series, unregistered_all_zero, census_agrees}`.

## Close rule
Close only with this subtask's own evidence, as typed references: `test:<crate>::<path>::<fn>`, `commit:<sha7>`, `record:<path>`, `ci:<run-id>@<sha7>` or an E id. Never a shared or generic reason (K.2 finding 4).

title: BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35
description:
_Plan row BD-341 (WP-03). Scope in one line: Guidance track record — the issuer's per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers and scored descriptively against first-published outcomes_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-332, BD-047, BD-048
- plan-deps: BD-332, BD-047, BD-048
- proposed-deps: BD-332, BD-343, NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions
- **Add BD-343.** Guidance is a range with no stated coverage. `FrozenForecast` stores only a Gaussian mean and standard deviation, and `evaluate_model` drops unresolved entries (FACT, `crates/fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:16–26, 111–160`). BD-343 adds an interval payload, cohorts and outcome vintages, so the scores must sit on it.
- **Keep BD-047 and BD-048 transitively**, through BD-343.
- **Add NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions.** Guidance is printed in PDFs, and the repository has no PDF reader.
- blocks: BD-342 (its S2 transcription only)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 1 (the M0 transcription target is the non-forecast answer to the "nothing new" kill; scores are M1)

## Background and why it matters
All three models in the idea duel ranked an idea about the issuer's guidance first.
- **The proposal.** Claude's CC-01 scored 730 and 865 from its rivals. After the rivals steelmanned it, those scores rose to 790 and 905.
- **The premise.** A filed or posted guidance statement carries a publication date that nobody can backdate, FrankenMining included. So the issuer's own forward statements are pre-registered forecasts (INV-008), years before FrankenMining existed.
- **Why it matters for M0.** It gives finance reviewers something new that does not depend on FrankenMining's own unscored forecasting skill.

The rivals attached four conditions:
1. no recalibration at n = 3 years;
2. descriptive scores with honest intervals;
3. transcription by two readers;
4. delivery privately to the sponsor first.

§21.6 also forbids any positive calibration claim before n ≈ 35 independent outcomes. One period across about 14 sites demonstrates the protocol, not skill.

## Goal
`fmine track-record --issuer barrick --json` reports, for each site, metric and year:
- the guidance range, its page and its publication date;
- the first-published outcome and whether it landed inside the range;
- descriptive aggregates: hit rate with a Clopper–Pearson interval, the side of each miss, and bias.

Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Current state
- **No code.** Nothing exists for guidance, and no guidance value is registered anywhere in the repository.
- **Known guidance facts.**
  - Lumwana 2026: AISC $3.40–3.75/lb (FACT, E586, AIF p.31).
  - North Mara 2026: 200–230 koz attributable, at $1,520–1,680/oz (FACT, E587 quoting AIF p.30).
- **The 2026 AIF** (dated 27 Feb 2026) was read by research pass W4 from a scratch download. It is not on disk in the corpus and not registered.
- **MD&As on disk.** The MD&As for Q1 2024 to Q2 2026 are in `corpus_of_input_docs/downloaded/mine_stats/`, but `sources.rs` registers only the 18 workbooks.
- **Documents missing from disk.** The documents that first published FY2023 and FY2024 guidance (early 2023 and early 2024) are not there (INFERENCE, from the file listing).
- **Outcomes.**
  - FY2024 and FY2025 outcomes are in the Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 Mine Stats (registered).
  - FY2023 appears only as a restated comparative in the Q4 2024 workbook, since its first publication (the Q4 2023 workbook) is not registered.

## Scope
**In:**
- source registration for the guidance documents;
- two-reader transcription;
- outcome binding;
- descriptive scores and a synthetic coverage test;
- a price-conditional split, gated per site;
- the verb.

**Out:**
- recalibration;
- site rankings when common shocks dominate;
- the guidance-at-risk nowcast (BD-342 holds the deductive version);
- any publication about the issuer.

## Design
**`GuidanceRecord`** fields:
- `issuer` and `subject`;
- `metric_key`, one of production_koz, aisc_usd_per_oz, tcc_usd_per_oz, c1_usd_per_lb, capex_usd_m;
- `basis{ownership: Attributable|Full, per_oz: Sold|Produced, credits: ByProduct|CoProduct}`;
- `period` (FY) and `value` (Range{lo,hi}, Point, AtMost or AtLeast);
- `assumptions{au_usd_oz, cu_usd_lb, …}`;
- `vintage` (Initial, Reaffirmed or Revised(n));
- `locator{doc, sha256, page, raw_token}` and `published_at`;
- `readers` (two role ids, no names).

"Equity share" guidance is attributable. It resolves against Mine Stats column C (attributable), never column B (100% basis) (E456).

**Two-reader rule.** Two independent transcriptions are diffed. A third role re-reads every disagreement, and only agreed rows enter the record.

**Outcomes** come through BD-343's cohorts:
- the default selector is the first-published vintage;
- restated values are scored separately;
- FY2023 is labelled `resolved_on_comparative_vintage`;
- divested or NOT_PUBLISHED members stay in the denominator as unresolved. Examples: Hemlo, sold 26 Nov 2025; Tongon, sold 1 Dec 2025 (E487); Loulo-Gounkoto 2025 (E818).

**Scores** are descriptive only.
- For a range [L, U], let m = (L + U)/2, h = (U − L)/2 and z = (y − m)/h.
- Report the hit rate k/n with a Clopper–Pearson interval, the share above the midpoint, and mean z with its interval.
- Also report n_eff, set to the number of years when the year effect dominates.
- Synthetic example: guidance [100, 120] and outcome 125 give z = +1.5, a miss on the high side.

**Price-conditional split** (HYPOTHESIS, gated per site). For an ad valorem royalty, the price-driven part of an AISC miss is r·(1 − P_assumed/P_realized).
- It is applied only where a per-site regression over the registered quarters supports royalty-per-ounce ∝ price. Otherwise the miss stays unsplit.
- The unconditional and conditional scores are always shown side by side.

**Delivery and disclosure.**
- The report goes privately to the sponsor first. FrankenMining publishes nothing about the issuer.
- Any external use of the report goes to counsel first, during the pre-release quiet period (§37.3).
- Every output is labelled "from public filings; no affiliation implied".

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every guidance and outcome value reproduces its cited page or cell, with two-reader agreement on 100% of entered rows.
2. Over at least 200 synthetic replicates with known coverage and bias, the 90% intervals for hit rate and bias cover the truth 85–95% of the time.
3. **Week-1 data gate.** Count the resolved years × sites with citations. If fewer than 3 × 10, ship single-site guidance cards for North Mara and Lumwana instead, and record that the gate fired.
4. FY2026 guidance is registered with its `published_at` before any FY2026 outcome is available.
5. Below n_eff ≈ 35, no output carries a calibration verdict.

## Tests
- **Parity.** Transcription fixtures carry their capture records and are never regenerated from the candidate.
- **Known answers.** A generator draws ranges with known c and μ and with year and site effects. The coverage criterion above applies.
- **Properties.**
  - Scores are invariant under exact unit changes.
  - The price split is the identity when P_realized = P_assumed.
  - An attributable guidance row is never scored against a 100% outcome (mutation test).
- **No hindsight.**
  - A guidance vintage is admissible only if `published_at` precedes the outcome's availability time (G-TIME-2).
  - The forecast horizon is part of the segment.
- **Denominator.** Withholding any outcome leaves n unchanged (BD-343 property).

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **The data gate fires.** Fall back to single-site cards.
- **Management reads the report as an attack.** Deliver privately and show the controllable score.
- **Common shocks dominate.** Refuse site rankings with FMINE-REF-104 (non-identifiable) and report the year-shock finding only.
- **Basis traps:** attributable against 100%, $/lb for Lumwana, regions under the versioned region map (E461), copper in kt (E463).
- **Never:**
  - claim "beats guidance" without an e-value;
  - treat implied figures as the issuer's own;
  - use non-public information.

## Subtasks
- **S1. Register guidance source documents.**
  - Contents: the AIFs and the full-year MD&As or releases that carry FY2023–FY2026 guidance, with URL, bytes, sha256 and `published_at`.
  - Also produce the week-1 data-gate count.
  - Acceptance: every needed document is either registered or listed as missing with its expected URL.
  - Deps: NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions.
- **S2. Two-reader transcription, FY2023–FY2026.**
  - Covers production, TCC or C1, AISC and capex for every gold and copper site.
  - Acceptance: criterion 1.
  - Deps: S1.
- **S3. Outcome binding.**
  - Contents: the FY blocks of the Q4 workbooks, BD-332 keys, the region map and unit rules, comparative-vintage labelling.
  - Deps: BD-332, S2.
- **S4. Descriptive scores**, with the synthetic generator and the coverage test.
  - Deps: BD-343, S3.
- **S5. Price-conditional split**, with the per-site proportionality test.
  - Deps: S4.
- **S6. `fmine track-record` verb.**

**Never:**

- register a document whose digest was not computed from bytes on disk;

So the Lumwana 2026 AISC row ($3.40–3.75/lb, E586) cannot be entered. Add `aisc_usd_per_lb` and `production_kt` (copper is printed in kt, E463).

**Files.** New module `crates/fmine-public/src/guidance.rs` (`pub mod guidance;` in `lib.rs`).

**`GuidanceRecord`** follows the dossier:
- `issuer` and `subject`, where the subject must be in `BARRICK_SUBJECTS` (`sources.rs:267`) or an S1-registered copper site;
- `metric_key`;
- `basis{ownership: Attributable|Full, per_oz: Sold|Produced, credits: ByProduct|CoProduct}`;
- `period` (FY) and `value` (`Range{lo,hi} | Point | AtMost | AtLeast`), held as exact rationals with a `step` taken from the printed digits;

- `vintage` (`Initial | Reaffirmed | Revised(n)`);
- `locator{doc, sha256, page, raw_token}` and `published_at`;
- `readers`: two role ids, never names.

**Rows.** The rows are NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions' `TranscribedValue`s.
- Reader A and reader B enter them as two independent Rust constant arrays (`BARRICK_GUIDANCE_ROWS_A` and `_B`).
- `agree(a, b) -> (Vec<GuidanceRecord>, Vec<Disagreement>)` accepts a row only if `raw_token`, `value`, `page` and the labels all match.
- Disagreements go to a third role for re-reading. They are never auto-resolved.

**Basis rule.** "Equity share" guidance is `Attributable` and resolves against Mine Stats column C (E456).

**Minimum rows.** These are also the single-site fallback cards if S1's gate fires.
- Lumwana FY2026 AISC: `Range[3.40, 3.75]` $/lb, step 0.01 (E586, AIF p.31).
- North Mara FY2026 production: `Range[200, 230]` koz attributable, raw token "200 - 230" (E587, AIF p.30).
- North Mara FY2026 AISC: `Range[1,520, 1,680]` $/oz (E587).

**Scope.** Production, TCC or C1, AISC and capex, for every gold and copper site in S1's registered documents, FY2023–FY2026. A cell with no row carries a named reason: not guided, document missing, or site divested.

**Registering the FY2026 issuer family (criterion 4).**
- Hand the FY2026 rows to BD-343 as `ForecastPayload::Interval{lo, hi, nominal: None}` under a separate model key, beside BD-067 and BD-068.
- The record time is the actual time of FrankenMining's registration, before Q4 2026 outcomes exist.
- Never set the record time to `published_at`: that would backdate FrankenMining's own act.

**Historical years (FY2023–FY2025).** Their outcomes are already public, so they must not go through `ForecastLedger::register` (`crates/fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:42`). They enter BD-343 cohorts as issuer-published forecasts. Their admissibility rests on the cited `published_at` preceding the outcome's availability (G-TIME-2).

**Handover to S3:** the agreed rows.

**Never:**
- regenerate the fixtures from the candidate;
- transcribe from markdown mirrors;
- transcribe any person's name;
- treat implied figures as the issuer's own.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Criterion 1.** Every entered row reproduces its cited page token: `raw_token`, page and labels. Two-reader agreement holds on 100% of entered rows.
- The disagreement list is empty, or every item carries a third-reader resolution record.
- Every row's doc sha256 equals a document registered in S1.
- The three E586 and E587 rows are present with the values above.
- **Criterion 4.** The FY2026 rows carry `published_at` and a registration time before any FY2026 outcome is available.

**Unit tests:**

- `test_guidance_token_known_answers`:
  - "200 - 230" gives [200, 230] with step 1;
  - "$3.40 to $3.75" gives [3.40, 3.75] with step 0.01;
  - "(708)" gives −708.
- `test_equity_share_rows_are_attributable` (E456, E587).
- `test_fy2026_issuer_family_registered_before_outcome_availability`.
- `test_reader_fields_are_role_ids`: matches a role-id pattern and contains no spaces.

**Negative controls:**

**Ignored real-file test.** `test_guidance_rows_bind_to_registered_pdfs` checks each row's doc digest on disk. It runs in BD-339's CI job.

title: BD-341.S3 [WP-03]: Outcome binding
description:

Subtask S3 of BD-341: "BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35". **Parent goal.** `fmine track-record --issuer barrick --json` reports, for each site, metric and year:
- the guidance range, its page and its publication date;
- the first-published outcome and whether it landed inside the range;

Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Work
**Goal.** Bind each agreed guidance row from S2 to its first-published FY outcome, keyed with BD-332's `PublicKey`. Hand the bound outcomes to BD-343 as `OutcomeEvent`s.

**Files.** `crates/fmine-public/src/guidance.rs`:
- `bind_outcome(rec: &GuidanceRecord, sources: &[LoadedSource], keys: &PublicKeyIndex) -> OutcomeBinding`;
- `OutcomeBinding` is either `Resolved{claim, vintage: FirstPublished | Comparative, at, sha256}` or `Unresolved{reason: NotPublished | Divested | Withheld | DefinitionChanged | NoCell}`.

**Where outcomes come from (FACT, registered):**
- **FY2024:** the FY blocks of `Barrick_Q4_2024_Mine_Stats.xlsx` (sha256 `f5e7db7c…`).
- **FY2025:** `Barrick_Q4_2025_Mine_Stats.xlsx` (`94f6692a…`).
- **Per-site FY AISC:** where the Mine Stats block lacks it, use the annual sheet of the Q4 AISC workbook (for example sheet `2025`, E691).
- **FY2023:** it exists only as a restated comparative in the Q4 2024 workbook. Its first publication (the Q4 2023 workbook) is not registered. Every FY2023 binding is labelled `resolved_on_comparative_vintage` and scored separately in S4.

**Rules:**
- **Ownership.** `Attributable` guidance binds only to Mine Stats column C, never to column B (100% basis) (E456). A cross-basis bind refuses with FMINE-REF-105 (basis mismatch).
- **Selector.** First-published by default. A later restatement is a separate `Restated` event, never an overwrite. That follows BD-343's E474 pattern: 1,479 first published, later shown as 1,474.
- **Units.**
  - Copper quantities are kt. Some 2024 Minestats4 labels say "millions of pounds" over kt values (E463); take the unit from the BD-332 unit registry, never from the label.
  - Lumwana costs are in $/lb.
  - Units never convert implicitly.
- **Regions.** Score sites only. A region-level row binds only under the region-map version of its vintage: Pueblo Viejo moves to North America from Q4 2025 and comparatives are restated (E461).
- **Denominator.** Divested, withheld or not-published members stay in the denominator as `Unresolved` (BD-343 `Missing{…}`):
  - Hemlo, sold 26 Nov 2025;
  - Tongon, sold 1 Dec 2025 (E487);
  - Loulo-Gounkoto 2025 (E818).
- **Loulo-Gounkoto FY2025 is OPEN.** FY2025 YTD cells exist: `Q4_2025:YTD!E16` 4,271 and `G16` 1,603, with FY sold equal to Q4 sold, 91 (W1-DR-07). Whether they form a full-year outcome is decided by BD-332's subject-status registry, which marks the site withheld for 2025Q1–Q3. The default is `Unresolved(DefinitionChanged)`.
- **Two families, two bases.** FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts target the 100% basis (§21.6, column B), while the issuer's guidance family is attributable. Both are scored on the same release, each on its own basis, and never cross-scored.

**Builds on:** BD-332 (keys and subject status) and S2 (rows).
**Hands over:** `OutcomeEvent::Published{value, vintage, locator, sha256}` or `Missing{reason}` per member, to S4 through BD-343 cohorts.

**Never:**
- pick the latest vintage silently;
- drop an unresolved member;
- treat a comparative vintage as first-published;
- default an unprinted ownership basis to 100%.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every `Resolved` outcome reproduces its cell, `<file>:<Sheet>!<Cell>`, and that file's registered sha256 (criterion 1, outcome side).
- Mutation: binding an attributable row to a column-B cell is refused, never scored.
- All FY2023 bindings carry `resolved_on_comparative_vintage`.
- Hemlo and Tongon FY2025 and Loulo-Gounkoto 2025 are `Unresolved` with their reasons. `n_members` is unchanged.
- No region row binds across region-map versions.

- `test_fy2023_outcome_labelled_comparative_vintage`;
- `test_divested_members_stay_in_denominator` (Hemlo, Tongon, Loulo-Gounkoto);
- `test_first_published_selector_ignores_later_restatement` (synthetic 1,479 → 1,474);
- `test_copper_quantity_unit_from_registry_not_label` (E463);
- `test_region_binding_respects_map_version` (E461);
- `test_unprinted_basis_refuses` (negative control).

**Ignored real-file test.** `test_guidance_outcomes_bind_to_q4_workbooks` runs in BD-339's CI job.

- Summary: `{"event":"guidance_outcomes_summary","members","resolved_first_published","resolved_comparative","unresolved_by_reason"}`.

## Close rule

title: BD-341.S4 [WP-03]: Descriptive scores
description:
## Context
Subtask S4 of BD-341: "BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** `fmine track-record --issuer barrick --json` reports, for each site, metric and year:
- the guidance range, its page and its publication date;
- the first-published outcome and whether it landed inside the range;
- descriptive aggregates: hit rate with a Clopper–Pearson interval, the side of each miss, and bias.

Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Work
**Goal.** Descriptive scores over BD-343 assessments: no recalibration, no ranking, no verdict.

**Files.** New module `crates/fmine-calib/src/guidance_scores.rs`.

**Builds on.** BD-343's `Assessment` (selector `FirstPublished`; restated values scored separately) and S3's bindings.

**Do not use `ForecastLedger::evaluate_model`** (`crates/fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:111`). It drops unresolved entries and sets `Calibrated`, `Biased` or `Overconfident` at any n ≥ 1.

**Per member.** `score_range(lo, hi, y) -> RangeScore{m, h, z, side: Below|Inside|Above, boundary: bool}`:
- m = (L + U)/2, h = (U − L)/2, z = (y − m)/h, in exact rationals (BD-340 `Rat`, or `ExactQty` plus BD-340's add and sub).
- Synthetic known answer: [100, 120] and y = 125 give z = +3/2, side Above.
- `boundary` marks an outcome whose printed rounding interval straddles L or U. It is reported, never hidden (DESIGN).
- `Point`, `AtMost` and `AtLeast` rows enter the hit rate only. Their z is undefined and is never computed.

**Aggregates per (metric, FY, vintage selector):**
- **Hit rate.** k/n with a two-sided 90% Clopper–Pearson interval.
  - Compute it by bisection on the exact binomial tail polynomial: no std transcendentals (NEW-det-portable-kernels).
  - Use NEW-irr-refuses' refusing root finder, so non-convergence refuses.
- **Share above the midpoint**, and the side of each miss.
- **Mean z** with an interval.
- **n_eff**, set to the number of years when the year effect dominates.
- **BD-343's whole-cohort bound** [k/n, (k + n_unresolved)/n]. Divested members stay in n.

**OPEN, decided by the coverage test.** Owner: the S4 implementer, signed off by the lead.
- The bias-interval method:
  - (a) a t-interval on per-year mean z, using a registered table of t quantiles;
  - (b) a Philox cluster bootstrap by year.
- The "year effect dominates" rule that sets n_eff.

**Synthetic generator.** `GuidanceWorld{sites, years, coverage c, bias μ, year_sd, site_sd, seed}`.
- It draws ranges with known c and μ, using `fmine_core::rand::PhiloxStream` (`rand.rs:78`) keyed by `RngKey`.
- It lives in test code in fmine-calib and is labelled synthetic. It moves to fmine-gen when BD-127 lands.
- Scenarios: no effects, year-dominant, and site-dominant.

**Flags.** Below n_eff ≈ 35 (§21.6) the flag is `Descriptive` or `Unscored`, never `Calibrated` (criterion 5).

**Hands over:** score records to S5 (conditional split) and S6 (rendering).

**Never:**
- recalibrate;
- claim "beats guidance" without an e-value;
- emit a calibration verdict.

- z known answer: [100, 120] with y = 125 gives exactly 3/2, a miss on the high side.
- **Criterion 2.** Run at least 200 replicates for each of the three scenarios. The 90% intervals for hit rate and bias cover the truth in 85–95% of replicates. The coverage and replicate count are reported per scenario.
- Scores are invariant under exact unit changes.
- Withholding any outcome leaves n unchanged.
- **Criterion 5.** No output below n_eff ≈ 35 carries a calibration verdict.

- `test_clopper_pearson_closed_form_edges`: k = 0, n = 10 gives upper 1 − 0.05^(1/10) ≈ 0.258866; k = n = 10 gives lower ≈ 0.741134 (INFERENCE, closed form). The test checks with `fmine_core::det` exp and ln.

title: BD-341.S5 [WP-03]: Price-conditional split
description:
## Context
Subtask S5 of BD-341: "BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** `fmine track-record --issuer barrick --json` reports, for each site, metric and year:
- the guidance range, its page and its publication date;
- the first-published outcome and whether it landed inside the range;
- descriptive aggregates: hit rate with a Clopper–Pearson interval, the side of each miss, and bias.

Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Work
**Status: HYPOTHESIS, gated per site.** The split always sits beside the unconditional score and never replaces it.

**Files:**
- `crates/fmine-public/src/guidance.rs`, which binds the royalty and price inputs as cited Claims;
- `crates/fmine-calib/src/guidance_scores.rs`, which adds a conditional score beside S4's.

**Rule (from the dossier).** For an ad valorem royalty, the price-driven part of an AISC miss is
p = r·(1 − P_assumed/P_realized).

Its inputs:
- **r: realised royalty per ounce for the site.** Mine Stats prints it per site, under "Costs per ounce ($/oz)" as "Royalties". The key is `royalties_usd_per_oz` (`planning/corpus/C1_barrick_public_stats.md:137`).
- **P_assumed: the guidance price assumption.** S2 transcribes it in `assumptions.au_usd_oz` or `cu_usd_lb`, with its page.
- **P_realized: the realised price for the same period.**
  - Whether a per-site realised price is printed is OPEN; the first reader of the MD&A decides.
  - If none is printed, use the company realised price from the MD&A, transcribed through NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions, and say so.

**Conditional score.** z_c = (y − p − m)/h, beside S4's z. Both always appear side by side.

**Scope.** The split applies only to AISC: gold AISC, and copper AISC, which includes royalties. It never applies to C1, which excludes royalties (C1 notes, A8), or to TCC (DESIGN).

**Per-site proportionality gate (DESIGN).** `royalty_proportional(site, quarters) -> Gate{beta_interval} | NotSupported{witness_quarters}`.
- Use the registered quarters, Q1 2024–Q2 2026.
- Test exact interval feasibility, in BD-340's style: is there a β such that every printed royalty (± half its step) equals β times the printed realised price (± half its step)?
- The feasible set is ∩_q [(r_q − ½)/(P_q + ½s), (r_q + ½)/(P_q − ½s)].
- An empty intersection refutes proportionality, and the miss stays unsplit for that site. Report the two quarters that witness the conflict.
- Whether a tolerance-based regression may replace the exact test is OPEN for the owner. Default: exact.

**Worked synthetic (labelled).** r = $100/oz, P_assumed = $1,500 and P_realized = $2,000 give p = 100·(1 − 3/4) = $25/oz.

**Context.** E607 says FY2025 company gold AISC of $1,637/oz was "slightly above guidance due to higher royalites driven by the higher realized gold price". That is a company statement, not a per-site split. Never cite it as a site's split.

**Builds on:** S4's `RangeScore`, and S2's `assumptions`.
**Hands over:** `ConditionalScore{p, z_c, gate}` to S6.

**Never:**
- split a site whose gate fails;
- infer P_assumed when guidance prints none (the row is unsplit, reason "no stated price assumption");
- present the conditional score alone;
- call the remainder "controllable" without the gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The split is the identity when P_realized = P_assumed: p = 0, so z_c = z.
- The synthetic example gives p = 25 exactly.
- Every site carries a gate result:
  - `Gate{beta_interval}` with its quarters cited; or
  - `NotSupported` with the conflicting quarters; or
  - unsplit with a reason.
- No output carries z_c without z.
- Every input (r, P_assumed, P_realized) cites a cell or a page and its sha256.

## Tests and logging
**Known answers:**
- `test_price_split_identity_when_prices_equal` (property).
- `test_price_split_synthetic_known_answer_25`.

**Gate:**
- `test_proportionality_gate_feasible_beta_interval`: synthetic quarters that are exactly proportional within rounding.
- `test_proportionality_gate_refuted_names_witness_quarters` (negative control).

**Refusal and scope:**
- `test_no_price_assumption_leaves_miss_unsplit`.
- `test_split_never_applied_to_c1_or_tcc`.

**Mutation check:**
- `test_conditional_score_never_rendered_alone`: removing z from the record fails validation.

**Ignored real-file test.** `test_royalty_proportionality_gate_real_quarters` runs in BD-339's CI job.
- Per site: `{"event":"price_split_gate","site","quarters","beta_lo","beta_hi","state","witness"}`, where `state` is supported, not_supported or no_assumption.
- Summary: `{"event":"price_split_summary","sites","supported","not_supported","no_assumption"}`.

## Close rule

description:
## Context
Subtask S6 of BD-341: "BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35". Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Work
**Goal.** `fmine track-record --issuer barrick [--site <subject>] [--json]` renders S2–S5 as the §30.1 envelope.

**Files and changes:**
- **`crates/fmine-cli/src/lib.rs`:**
  - add `CliCommand::TrackRecord{issuer, site: Option<String>}` to the enum at line 19;
  - parse it in `parse_args` (line 118), where an unknown issuer is a usage error with exit 2;
  - dispatch it in `execute_command` (line 211);
  - add `"track-record --issuer <issuer>"` to the robot-docs verb list (line 284).
- **`registries/verbs.toml`:** `[[verb]] path = "track-record"`, `subsystem = "Plumb"`, `mutates_authority = false`.
- **`crates/fmine-public/src/guidance.rs`:** `run_track_record(profile, root) -> Result<TrackRecordReport, Refusal>`.
  - It loads the registered workbooks (`load_registered_sources`, `lib.rs:126`) and the registered PDFs.
  - A missing or altered file refuses with FMINE-REF-502, naming the file (exit 8).

**Envelope (§30.1).** One event per line:
- one `track_record.row` event per (site, metric, FY, vintage);
- one `track_record.summary` event per (metric, FY, selector);
- a final `track_record.run`.

Each event carries:
- `flags`: all four false, with no setter (INV-002);
- `certificate`: the blake3 digest of the canonical rows (`Encoder` frame, rows sorted);
- `warnings` and `next_actions`.

If BD-329's envelope rewrite has not landed, use today's `Envelope` (`lib.rs:34`), with the events in `payload`.

**Citations (BD-329 shapes).**
- Guidance values are `extracted`, with `at` = `<doc>:p<page>:<row>/<col>` and the sha256.
- Outcomes are `extracted` cells.
- z, hit rate and the Clopper–Pearson bounds are `derived`, with rule ids such as `guidance.z`, `guidance.hit_rate.cp90` and `guidance.price_split`.
- Counts use the `count` shape.

**Required text.** Every output carries "from public filings; no affiliation implied". The `no_claim` text holds no digits, because BD-329 rule (e) rejects digits in prose. Proposed wording: "Describes how the issuer's published per-site guidance compared with its first-published outcomes. Descriptive only: no calibration verdict below the registered minimum effective sample size, no site ranking, no forecast."

**Data gate.** If S1's gate fired, the verb renders only the North Mara and Lumwana single-site cards (E586, E587), with `gate_fired: true` and the counts.

**Delivery.** The output stays on stdout, with no network and no files written. It goes privately to the sponsor first. External use goes to counsel during the pre-release quiet period (§37.3).

**Builds on:** S4, plus S5 when that has landed. The conditional score is shown only beside the unconditional one.

**Never print:**
- a calibration verdict;
- "beats guidance";
- a site ranking (a request for one refuses with FMINE-REF-104);
- any implied figure presented as the issuer's own.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The verb is registered in `verbs.toml` and robot-docs, and `cargo run -p xtask -- check-all` passes.
- Envelope golden test: the four flags are false; the `no_claim` text and the no-affiliation label are present; BD-329's validator finds no uncited number.
- Without the corpus, the verb exits 8 and names every missing registered file.
- On the gate-fired path, exactly two site cards render.
- Reruns are byte-identical.
- No output text contains a calibration verdict or a ranking.

- `test_track_record_ranking_request_refuses`.

**Ignored real-file test.** `test_cli_track_record_barrick_real_files` runs in BD-339's CI job (`-p fmine-cli -- --ignored`).
