title: BD-336 [WP-10]: Metallurgical-balance and sampler-record import for the recovery-led GATE-DATA-03 route (§37.3 M2)
description:
_Plan row BD-336 (WP-10). Scope in one line: Metallurgical-balance and sampler-record import for the recovery-led GATE-DATA-03 route_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-187
- plan-deps: BD-187   proposed-deps: BD-187, BD-186, BD-137, BD-309; BD-133 for the synthetic e2e only
- blocks: BD-204 (existing edge, K.6)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 2 (it blocks BD-204 on the 29-bead critical path, but no site data can exist before GATE-DATA-01 at month 4; it must be ready by month 6)

## Background and why it matters
The M2 pilot (plan §37.3) prefers **Lumwana**, Barrick's only wholly owned operating mine. There the finding is **recovery-led**, not grade-led:
- every 2025–26 quarter sits 1.7–2.7 points below the 2013–22 grade–recovery relation (INFERENCE, E566);
- that is 2.4–3.4% of output, roughly $30–57M/yr at $4.00–5.50/lb (INFERENCE, E567);
- the public metal balance reproduces the printed recovery within ±1.5 points, so the gap is not a print artefact (E127).

The pre-registered deliverable attributes the grade-normalised gap among three causes: measurement (head and tail sampling, assay), ore type (fresh against transitional) and operations.

GATE-DATA-03 therefore has two thresholds (R7-C084, R7-C102; §34.4):
- the **recovery-led** threshold, which is this bead's file set:
  - the monthly metallurgical balance;
  - head, tail and concentrate sampler and assay records;
  - concentrate shipment and settlement assays;
  - fresh/transitional tags on feed;
  - the monthly reconciliation pack;
- the grade-led threshold, which needs block and GC models, dispatch tonnages, surveys and cost-centre extracts.

On the recovery-led route BD-204 does not wait on BD-188, BD-189 or BD-194. It waits on this bead (K.6 adds the edge BD-204 ← BD-336, and with it WP-12 → WP-10). GATE-TOUCH-03 gains a recovery-led variant: parity with the site's monthly metallurgical balance and recovery statement, not with F1/F2/F3.

## Goal
Import the recovery-led file set through the quarantine pipeline, with every column declared. Then reproduce the site's own monthly recovery statement from the imported records: each month is either reproduced within its printed rounding or listed as a cited discrepancy.

## Current state (FACT unless marked)
- No `fmine-plant` crate exists. The P754 balance (BD-177), the flowsheet types (BD-175) and the reconciliation engine (BD-149) are all open.
- `fmine-io` reads XLSX and HTML tables only (`crates/fmine-io/CONTRACT.md` §4; `crates/fmine-io/src/lib.rs:45`). It has no CSV reader. BD-187 (own CSV/Excel readers), BD-185 (quarantine pipeline) and BD-186 (`io_dialects.toml`) are open.
- No site data exist, and site data by month 7 is not assumed (plan §34.4; E599). This bead is an M2 design with no code yet.
- The plan names no bead for GATE-TOUCH-03's recovery-led variant. BD-206 owns GATE-TOUCH-03 only as F1/F2/F3 parity.

## Scope
**In:**
- dialect rows for the five recovery-led file families;
- record types;
- quadruple timestamps;
- parity recomputation against the site statement;
- import reports with explained rejections.

**Out:**
- the reconciliation posterior (BD-207);
- sampler bias models (BD-178);
- the historian and LIMS (GATE-DATA-04);
- any personal data.

## Design (DESIGN)
- **Record types** (in `fmine-plant::import`, layer K2; parsing in `fmine-io`):
  - `MetBalanceMonth{period, streams: [StreamRow{stream: Feed|Concentrate|Tail|Other, dry_t, grades: [{species: CuT|CuAS|Au|…, value, unit}], contained, method: Measured|Calculated|Reconciled}], stated_recovery{value, printed_precision, method_label}}`;
  - `SamplerRecord{sampler_id, stream, lot, increments, cut_interval}`;
  - `AssayRecord{sample_id, lab, method, batch, certificate, crm_results, value, detection_limit}`;
  - `Shipment{lot, wet_t, moisture, dry_t, assays: {seller, buyer, umpire}, settlement}`;
  - `FeedTag{period_or_lot, fresh_fraction, transitional_fraction}`.
- **Declarations and stamps.**
  - Every column has a dialect row giving unit, basis (wet or dry; total or acid-soluble Cu) and support. A column without one stays `UNREGISTERED` (FMINE-REF-107).
  - Raw tokens are kept.
  - Every record carries a `QuadTemporalStamp`.
- **Quarantine.** Bytes land read-only in `ImportQuarantineRegion` (no TIME, RANDOM or REMOTE), each citing its CAS digest. Rejections are explained one by one in the import report.
- **Personal data.** Sampler and lab logs can name operators. A dialect row marks such columns `Personal`. They are never imported, and Zambia's DPA 2021 s.70 keeps personal data in country (E514).
- **Parity.** For each month, recompute:
  - contained metal per stream (dry t × grade);
  - the mass-measured recovery, conc metal ÷ feed metal;
  - the two-product recovery, R = c(f − t) / (f(c − t));
  - check-in against check-out, kept separate as MCF in and out (§17.5).

  Compare the result with the stated recovery on its printed rounding interval, using the statement's declared method:
  - declared method reproduced: state i;
  - no method declared and exactly one formula reproduces: state ii (reconstructed);
  - both or neither formula reproduces: state iv, or state iii with a certificate.

  The import never adds a tolerance that the site did not state.
- **Worked example (synthetic, labelled).** Feed is 2,000,000 t at 0.60% Cu (12,000 t Cu). Concentrate is 50,000 t at 22% (11,000 t). Tail is 1,950,000 t at 0.05% (975 t).
  - The mass-measured recovery is 11,000 ÷ 12,000 = 91.67%.
  - The two-product recovery is 22 × 0.55 ÷ (0.60 × 21.95) = 91.88%.
  - 25 t of metal is unaccounted.

  A statement printing 91.9% matches only the two-product method, so the month is state ii if no method is declared. A statement printing 91.7% matches only the mass method.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each of the five file families from the pilot site imports with zero `UNREGISTERED` columns used in parity, and each rejection is explained.
- Each historical month (the target is 2024Q1–2027Q1; §37.3) has a parity state. Every month not in state i or ii names its certificate or the document that would close it.
- The import report and the parity table regenerate byte-identically from the same snapshot.
- No personal column crosses the import boundary.

## Tests
- **Unit:**
  - the two formulas against BD-137's P754 and two-product fixtures;
  - rounding-interval comparison;
  - wet-to-dry conversion with moisture.
- **Property:**
  - permuting the order of rows and files leaves parity unchanged;
  - unit relabelling (t and kt; % and g/t where valid) leaves states unchanged.
- **Known answers:** the synthetic month above; a synthetic site pack from BD-133 with seeded head-sampler bias, where parity must still reproduce the site's (biased) statement, because parity is not truth.
- **Negative and mutation:**
  - drop a column's dialect row: refused;
  - swap the conc and tail grades: a state iii certificate appears;
  - a statement with an unstated method: no silent choice;
  - an operator-name column: refused at import.
- **e2e:** `fmine import` over a synthetic Lumwana-dialect snapshot. Structured logs per file (digest, rows, rejections) and per month (state, formula, interval).

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **The site's balance uses reconciled masses that we cannot reproduce from raw records.** Import the reconciled balance as an `Assertion` with parity on its own arithmetic, and flag that raw-to-reconciled parity is unavailable.
- **The site supplies only PDFs.** Use cited-mode entry by two readers.
- **Lumwana declines.** The bead still serves the alternates; North Mara is grade-led and does not need it.

## Recommended plan changes
1. Add BD-186 (dialects) and BD-137 (P754 fixtures) as dependencies. Parity needs both.
2. Add BD-309 (stamps) as a dependency, after the stamp shape is fixed (see BD-344's note on the plan–code field mismatch).
3. Give GATE-TOUCH-03's recovery-led variant an owner. Either widen BD-206's done-when to "F1/F2/F3 parity, or monthly metallurgical-balance parity via BD-336", or add a small bead.

## References
- Plan: §37.3 M2 (lines 7672–7740); §34.4 GATE-DATA-03 (7352–7386); §17.5 (3205–3236); §32.1; K.6; bead row line 8182.
- Evidence: E127, E514, E566, E567, E570, E599 (`planning/research/W4_m2_site_and_data_access.md:609–642`).
- Claims: R7-C084, R7-C102.
- Code: `crates/fmine-io/CONTRACT.md`.
acceptance_criteria:
Plan done-when (§39 row BD-336): Site's monthly balance and recovery statement imported with parity

- Each of the five file families from the pilot site imports with zero `UNREGISTERED` columns used in parity, and each rejection is explained.
- Each historical month (the target is 2024Q1–2027Q1; §37.3) has a parity state. Every month not in state i or ii names its certificate or the document that would close it.
- The import report and the parity table regenerate byte-identically from the same snapshot.
- No personal column crosses the import boundary.

K.6 edge kept: bd-204 <- BD-336. The recovery-led GATE-TOUCH-03 variant now has its own bead, which depends on this one.

title: NEW [WP-01]: GATE-FSIM-DRIFT: quarterly diff of every lifted frankensim region against its pinned commit
description:
## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- plan-deps: none (plan §27 defines the gate; no bead row owns it)   proposed-deps: NEW-lift-provenance-truth
- blocks: none

Type and priority rationale: priority: 3 (M1 suite gate; little to diff until NEW-lift-provenance-truth leaves only true lifts with pinned commits)

## Background and why it matters
FrankenMining lifts code from the sibling engine FrankenSim instead of depending on it (plan §27.1: "Lift-only", FD-FSIM-00; any Cargo dependency waits for GATE-FSIM-RECONV). Lifted code can drift from upstream bug fixes. Plan §27 defines **GATE-FSIM-DRIFT** (quarterly): diff each lifted source at frankensim HEAD against its pinned commit; any upstream change inside a lifted region opens a bead within 10 working days; the decision (re-lift, or no-op with a reason) is recorded. Plan F8 lists it as the control for "lifted-code drift or an upstream bug". No bead row owns it (§39), and the suite table puts it at M1.

FACT (2026-10-29 research, recorded in NEW-lift-provenance-truth): five of the eight files registered as "lifted" share at most two lines with their claimed upstream file, and the rand row hashes `lib.rs` while the code came from `philox.rs`. A drift check over false provenance would diff unrelated files. So this bead waits for that correction.

## Process-rule answers (AGENTS RULE 0.1)
1. Consumer: the agent who re-lifts, and the M1 suite gate record.
2. Gate enforced: GATE-FSIM-DRIFT.
3. Defect class: a known upstream bug fix not carried into a lifted copy (plan F8).
4. Retirement: when no lifted frankensim region remains (all replaced by own code or by a Cargo dependency after GATE-FSIM-RECONV).

## Goal
`cargo run -p xtask -- check-lift-drift --upstream <path-to-frankensim-checkout>` reads `registries/lifts.toml` (source repo, path, line range or symbol, pinned commit, lifted blake3), diffs each region between the pinned commit and upstream HEAD, and prints one line per lift: `unchanged`, `changed (n lines)` with the diff, or `missing upstream`. A scheduled CI job runs it quarterly and fails on any `changed` row without a recorded decision.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every lifts.toml row is checked; a seeded upstream change in a test fixture repository is reported as `changed`, and an unrelated change outside the region as `unchanged`.
2. A decision file (or the bead it opens) records re-lift or no-op with reason per changed row; the CI job passes only when every changed row has one.
3. Runs without network access when given a local checkout; quotes upstream commits, never working-tree state (frankensim's working tree has had uncommitted deletions: E824).

## Tests
Unit tests on region extraction (line range and symbol); an e2e over a temporary git repository built in the test with two commits; structured output, one JSON line per lift.

## Risks
Keep it one xtask subcommand plus one CI schedule; no dashboard, no new registry beyond fields lifts.toml already needs.

title: BD-353 [WP-14]: Compensation-formula exposure: exact piecewise evaluator of a scheme formula over admitted metric definitions and rounding intervals; synthetic first, then one publicly disclosed formula; no personal data
description:
_Plan row BD-353 (WP-14). Scope in one line: Compensation-formula exposure: an exact piecewise evaluator over admitted metric definitions, with no personal data_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-340, BD-061
- plan-deps: BD-340, BD-061   proposed-deps: BD-340, BD-061, BD-332 (metric vintage keys)
- blocks: none

Type and priority rationale: priority: 3 (serves the compensation-committee reader R7 added; M1 synthetic slice; the public case may end in an ambiguity warning)

## Background and why it matters
R7 added the compensation (remuneration) committee as a reader (§3; K.3 #2; R7-C139, R7-C140). Its question is not what a metric *is*, but whether the admitted definitions, adjustments and rounding support **one** scheme-level performance factor, or whether the ambiguity can cross a threshold.

**Why a point is not enough.** A step or kink in a scheme turns a small metric ambiguity into a large factor ambiguity. A capped portion can absorb a large change. A midpoint evaluation hides both.

**What the plan already has.** §23.6 prices the economic sacrifice of KPI constraints. It does not evaluate the scheme function itself. The duel's Codex blind spot BS-COD-02 (self 740; orchestrator 650; K.5 row 17) proposes exactly that, synthetic first.

**The public case (FACT unless marked).**
- Barrick's 2026 Circular scorecard gives gold AISC an 18.75% weight. The row prints $1,565/oz, $1,352/oz and $1,423/oz (E605).
- The reported FY2025 AISC was $1,637/oz (E607).
- The Circular promises to disclose adjustments, but shows none for AISC. The $1,637 → $1,423 bridge is therefore undisclosed (INFERENCE, E608; OPEN-BULL-1).
- GEO in the scorecard uses fixed reserve prices of $1,500/oz and $3.25/lb (E606), so that component's basis is reproducible.

## Goal
A pure, exact evaluator of a scheme formula over admitted metric definitions and rounding intervals. It returns the *image set* of the scheme index and the clause and branch behind each possible value. It works on a synthetic scheme first, then on one publicly disclosed formula if its terms suffice. Otherwise it gives an ambiguity warning naming the missing clause.

## Current state (FACT)
- No Helm crates exist (`fmine-capital`, `fmine-econ`). `fmine-metrics` holds versioned decks and GEO (`crates/fmine-metrics/src/lib.rs:88–130`). BD-061 (the metric engine) is closed with the generic reason. BD-340 exists only in the plan text.
- `ExactQty` has mul and div only. Exact rational add and compare must come from BD-340's type (`crates/fmine-units/src/lib.rs:275–332`).
- No scheme data, no evaluator. This is an M1 design.

## Scope
**In:**
- a scheme specification: components, weights, schedules, inequality direction, caps, and the metric definition id plus vintage plus adjustment policy;
- an exact piecewise evaluator over intervals and branches;
- breakpoint enumeration;
- clause attribution;
- one public capture attempt.

**Out:**
- salaries, grants, individual achievement, names, or any person-linked id;
- estimating anyone's pay;
- deciding whether a restatement changes an award or triggers clawback;
- pricing safety gates (hard, never priced; G-HELM-1);
- payroll administration.

## Design (DESIGN)
- **Spec.** A `SchemeSpec` lists `components[k]`, each with:
  - `weight` (exact rational);
  - `metric: MetricRef{definition_id, vintage, adjustment_policy}`;
  - `direction` (HigherBetter or LowerBetter);
  - `schedule`: breakpoints with payout factors and an interpolation rule (Step or Linear);
  - an explicit inequality at every breakpoint (≥ or >);
  - `cap` and `floor`.

  The spec text and its structured reading carry a role-reviewed version. An unknown adjustment policy stays `Unresolved`. It never defaults to the public non-GAAP definition.
- **Evaluation.**
  - Each component's admitted input is a set of intervals, one per definition branch, each widened by its rounding interval.
  - The image of a piecewise-linear schedule over an interval is computed exactly:
    - evaluate the interval endpoints and every breakpoint inside the interval;
    - for Step rules, add both one-sided limits at each step.
  - The output is a finite union of points and intervals. Rules may be non-monotone; endpoints alone are not assumed to suffice.
  - Components combine by Minkowski sum over the weighted images, with branches kept apart.
- **Output.**
  - The image set.
  - Its breakpoints crossed.
  - For each piece, the branch and clause responsible.
  - The output is never collapsed to a midpoint, and a range that straddles a threshold is never printed as a point.
- **Known answer (INFERENCE; BS-COD-02).** Fixed components contribute 0.75. One component of weight 0.25 pays 0 below a normalised achievement of 0.90 and 1 at or above it (≥). The admitted achievement is [0.89, 0.91].
  - The image is **{0.75, 1.00}**: two points, not the interval 0.75–1.00.
  - The midpoint answer, 1.00, would hide the threshold.
- **Public attempt.**
  - Capture the 2026 Circular's scorecard formula and definitions by two-reader cited transcription.
  - Admit the GEO component if its schedule and interpolation rule are stated. That they are stated has not been checked here (OPEN).
  - For gold AISC, the expected result is the ambiguity warning: "adjustment from reported $1,637 to scored $1,423 not disclosed (E608)", with the Circular page that would close it. No factor is printed for that component.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every threshold boundary in the synthetic schemes is enumerated, and no range across a threshold is reported as a point (K.5 row 17).
- The synthetic known answer above reproduces as a two-point set.
- The public attempt either reproduces the disclosed factor with hashes and locators, or names precisely the clause that prevents reproduction.
- A data-scope check finds no field in the spec or the outputs that can hold a person identifier.

## Tests
- **Unit:**
  - step and linear schedules;
  - ≥ against > at ties;
  - caps and floors;
  - lower-is-better metrics (AISC);
  - Minkowski sum over components.
- **Exhaustive:** a small rational grid evaluated against an independently authored rule table, covering every breakpoint, tie, cap, overlapping branch, wrong metric vintage and rounding interval that straddles a threshold.
- **Property and metamorphic:**
  - a pure unit change (for example $/oz expressed in cents) preserves the image;
  - narrowing the input never enlarges the image.
- **Negative:**
  - an unresolved adjustment policy yields `Unresolved`, not a number;
  - a wrong metric vintage is refused.
- **e2e:** an evaluation of a synthetic scheme, with structured logs `{component, branch, interval, breakpoints_crossed, image}`.

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **Nothing reproducible.** If no disclosed formula can be reproduced from public terms, ship the ambiguity warning only (K.5).
- **Out of bounds.** Kill if the useful workflow needs personal remuneration data or automatic legal interpretation. Do not build a generic compensation engine.
- **Never:**
  - name an executive;
  - estimate an award;
  - say an award was wrong;
  - imply any Barrick affiliation.

## References
- Plan: §3 (compensation-committee row), §23.6 (lines 5193–5213), OPEN-BULL-1 (4789), K.3 #2, K.5 row 17, bead row line 8262.
- Duel: `planning/duel/WIZARD_BLINDSPOTS_COD.md:104–175` (BS-COD-02).
- Evidence: E605–E608 (`planning/research/W5_figure_verification.md:322–329`).
- Claims: R7-C139, R7-C140.

description:

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 0 (K.2 pre-push step 1; DONE in commit 543df53, closed with its own evidence)

## Background and why it matters
Round 7 (plan Appendix K.2, finding 1; claims R7-C001, R7-C011, R7-C058, R7-C059, R7-C065) found that the first M0 commit (`68e7091`) did not read Barrick's data at all.
- Every figure that `fmine assure public --issuer barrick` printed came from a workbook built in code (a "stand-in") or from literals.
- When a registered file was missing or unreadable, the reader silently substituted the stand-in, file by file, and exited 0.
- With the real workbooks present under the expected names, the command refused (FMINE-REF-502, no "Gold AISC" sheet).
- Changing an input cell left the output and the state root byte-identical. The output did not depend on the inputs at all.

Finding 2 (R7-C002–R7-C006, R7-C054, R7-C159) showed the stand-in's figures were wrong as Barrick figures:
- FY2025 AISC printed 1,638 against a published $1,637/oz.
- 3,255 is attributable production, not ounces sold (3,318).
- The reserve-replacement inputs had been solved to hit 190% and 504%.
- None of the stand-in's 41 explicit values sat at a published coordinate.

Under the owner's loss function, a wrong figure under an issuer's name is the costliest M0 failure. That is why this was step 1 of the pre-push list.

## Goal
1. A missing or unreadable registered file makes the run exit non-zero, naming the file.
2. No in-code workbook can be mistaken for an issuer's data. Synthetic data run in a separate lane whose output says `synthetic` and can never count toward GATE-BULL-01 (the M0 gate on reproducing Barrick's published figures).
3. The four stand-in tests are replaced by labelled synthetic tests plus a real-file run. None is deleted or weakened.

## What was done (FACT, commit 543df53, 2026-10-29)
**`fmine-io`: both fallbacks removed.**
- `build_canonical_barrick_xlsx_bytes()` is gone (`crates/fmine-io/src/zip_inflate.rs`).
- `Workbook::from_file` returns `IoError::FileRead{path, detail}` instead of substituting (`crates/fmine-io/src/xlsx.rs`).
- A generic `build_minimal_xlsx` writer exists for synthetic workbooks. It writes no issuer bytes.

**`fmine-public`: refusal and synthetic lane.**
- `load_registered_sources` refuses with FMINE-REF-502 (exit 8). The refusal names every missing, altered or unreadable registered file: "N of 18 registered barrick workbooks unusable under …; missing: …; digest mismatch: …; unreadable: …".
- `synthetic.rs` holds the synthetic lane: invented sites "Site A–G" and "Region North", with seeded known answers for every state of the identity ledger.
- `Lane::Synthetic` reports `"lane":"synthetic"` and `gate_eligible:false`.

**`fmine-cli`.**
- `fmine assure public --synthetic` runs the synthetic lane.
- `--issuer` plus `--synthetic`, a missing `--issuer`, and an unknown issuer are usage errors (exit 2).

**`fmine-metrics`.**
- The mislabelled "Barrick" tests (GEO, reserve replacement, LMDI) are relabelled synthetic, with honest known answers.
- The price decks were corrected to the 2026 Circular (E606).

## Acceptance Criteria
_the plan's done-when, with evidence_
1. "A missing or unreadable registered file exits non-zero naming it":
   - `fmine-public` `missing_corpus_refuses_naming_every_registered_file`;
   - `fmine-public/tests/registry.rs` `altered_registered_file_is_refused_with_both_digests`;
   - `fmine-io` `test_missing_file_is_an_error_never_a_stand_in`;
   - the `fmine-cli` refusal test (exit 8, names `Barrick_Q2_2026_AISC.xlsx`).
2. "Synthetic output is labelled and excluded": `fmine-public` `synthetic_lane_reproduces_every_seeded_answer`, plus the `fmine-cli` synthetic end-to-end test. Both assert `lane=synthetic` and `gate_eligible=false`.
3. Real-file run: the ignored test `barrick_real_files_match_the_independent_reader` passes locally on the 18 workbooks (MOR_CASE E820–E822).

## Tests

- The two ignored real-file tests need the gitignored corpus. BD-339 builds the kit and CI job that runs them anywhere.

## Risks and follow-ups

title: BD-352 [WP-02]: Evidence-origin accounting: origin identities and typed relations (publication copy, superseding publication, repeated reading, replicate, new observation, shared systematic-error group)
description:
_Plan row BD-352 (WP-02). Scope in one line: Evidence-origin accounting: origin identities and typed relations, so that a reprint never narrows an interval_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-042
- plan-deps: BD-042   proposed-deps: BD-042, BD-041, BD-046 (all closed with the generic reason; this bead must re-verify what it uses), BD-332 for the public-lane relations
- blocks: none as a hard edge. BD-346 (JV mirror) and BD-351 should read origin relations, as soft links.

Type and priority rationale: priority: 3 (contested in the duel; M1–M2; its value depends on mapping quality for one narrow record family)

## Background and why it matters
FrankenMining composes evidence by weakest link (NL-1, NL-2) and records derivation edges in a provenance DAG (BD-046). That says *how* a number was derived. It does not say whether two pieces of evidence are *independent*, and the difference changes uncertainty:
- **Copies.** Three reports quoting one assay are three publications of one observation, not three assays.
- **Shared errors.** Two distinct assays may share a batch calibration error.
- **Common random numbers.** These align computations but do not make evidence independent.

The duel's COD-03 (rival scores 620 and 805, contested; K.5 row 16) asks for origin identities and typed relations that change model admission and intervals, not just a source count shown to humans. The public lane already has the cases:
- **E692:** a superseding publication. The 2024 GEO net change was printed 6.7, then 79.
- **E698:** two publications of one roll-forward with two rounding conventions (deck and MD&A).
- **JV filings (BD-346):** separately audited JV-partner filings may reuse the same operator measurement, so agreement between them is not independent confirmation (COD's critique of CC-06).

## Goal
Each piece of evidence carries:
- an origin identity;
- typed relations: publication copy, superseding publication, repeated reading, technical replicate, new observation, shared systematic-error group.

A first statistical kernel must then show two things:
- the batch-bias variance σ_b² + σ_ε²/n is reproduced;
- copying or reordering publications never narrows any interval.

## Current state (FACT)
- `compose_binary` (`crates/fmine-claim/src/lib.rs:267–325`) takes the weakest-link evidence class and knowledge state, joins confidentiality, and unions parents, anchors and UU terms. The caller supplies the derived value and its `Representation`, so no variance is composed and nothing knows about origins.
- `ClaimDag` (`lib.rs:350–430`) holds parent edges and staleness only.
- `cholesky_solve` exists (`crates/fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs:18`). It is the seam for a small generalised least squares (GLS) kernel.
- BD-042 is closed with the shared generic close reason (K.2 finding 4). The NL tests exist in `fmine-claim`'s test module. The §7.1/§7.2 type mismatch (K.2 finding 7) is open.
- No origin types exist. This is an M1–M2 design.

## Scope
**In:**
- `OriginId` and the relation enum in `fmine-claim`;
- manual assertion of relations, with review;
- a Gaussian measurement kernel for independent noise plus a declared group bias (in `fmine-calib` or `fmine-numerics`);
- the unknown-dependence rule;
- the public-lane relations for E692 and E698.

**Out:**
- fuzzy or automatic matching;
- spatial covariance (§13, §20 own it);
- effective-sample-size claims shown as facts.

## Design (DESIGN)
- **Origin identity.**
  - Physical records: sample id, assay run, certificate and batch.
  - Public lane: the originating table cell or page, with later publications linked to it by an *asserted* relation.

  Matching numbers or text never establishes identity. A proposed match stays an `Assertion` until a reviewer accepts it.
- **Relations and their effect:**
  - *publication copy*: same origin, adds no observation;
  - *superseding publication*: the later vintage is current and both are kept;
  - *repeated reading* of one measurement: not independent;
  - *technical replicate*: shares sample-preparation error, has independent analytical error;
  - *new observation*: independent;
  - *shared systematic-error group*: a declared covariance block.
- **Kernel.** y_i = μ + b_{g(i)} + ε_i, with Σ = σ_ε²·I + σ_b²·Z·Zᵀ.
  - GLS estimate of μ, with Var(μ̂) = (1ᵀ Σ⁻¹ 1)⁻¹ computed through `cholesky_solve`.
  - Publication copies are collapsed to their origin *before* the kernel sees them.
- **Unknown dependence.** If the relation between two readings is unknown, never assume ρ = 0. With equal variances, Var(mean) = σ²(1 + (n − 1)ρ)/n is largest at ρ = 1. The kernel therefore reports the conservative σ² and states the assumption that would license narrowing.
- **Rounding versus measurement.** Two publication copies of one deterministic printed quantity may legitimately *intersect* their rounding intervals, because that identifies one number (E698: the split near 3.65/1.75 is INFERENCE). That never reduces the *measurement* uncertainty of the underlying estimate. The two kinds of interval are kept in separate fields.
- **Worked example (synthetic).** σ_b = 0.05 g/t and σ_ε = 0.20 g/t.

  | Case | Var(mean) | sd (g/t) |
  |---|---|---|
  | n = 4, one batch | 0.0025 + 0.04/4 = 0.0125 | 0.112 |
  | n = 16, one batch | 0.005 | 0.071 |
  | n → ∞, one batch | floor at 0.0025 | 0.05 |
  | n = 4, each reprinted once (8 rows) | 0.0125 | 0.112 |
  | the same 8 rows treated naively as iid, bias ignored | 0.005 | 0.071 (the bug this bead prevents) |
  | two independent batches of 4 | 0.00625 | 0.079 |

## Acceptance Criteria
- The batch-bias known answer σ_b² + σ_ε²/n is reproduced analytically. Empirical coverage of the nominal interval lies within Monte Carlo error over ≥ 200 sealed-truth replicates.
- No copy, reprint or reordering of publications narrows any interval.
- An independent batch narrows the interval as the model says.
- Origin ids and relations are canonical inputs: changing them changes the result's identity.
- The independently reviewed fixture family has zero false automatic merges, because there are no automatic merges.

## Tests
- **Unit:**
  - each relation's effect;
  - the unknown-dependence rule;
  - separation of rounding and measurement intervals.
- **Property:**
  - duplicate any subset of publications k times: the measurement interval is unchanged;
  - permute rows: identical results;
  - add an independent batch: the variance does not increase.
- **Known answers:**
  - the table above;
  - E698 as two copies of one origin: the rounding interval intersects, the measurement interval does not narrow;
  - E692 as a superseding publication: current = 79, the 6.7 row kept.
- **Positive and negative controls:**
  - legitimate same-sample technical replicates are not collapsed;
  - conflicting superseding values stay `conflicted`, not averaged.
- **e2e:** a synthetic Corebox batch set with structured logs `{origins, relations, groups, var_model, interval}`.

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **Overlap with domain models.** If existing domain covariance models (§12.5, §20) already cover the use, keep only the schema and the reprint guard (K.5).
- **Fragile matching.** Kill any generic independence score that depends on document similarity or on shared-error parameters nobody can justify.
- **Misleading interface.** A misleading "independent sources" display is worse than none. Show dependency descriptions, never automatic effective sample sizes.

## References
- Plan: §7.1–7.3 (lines 620–675), K.5 row 16, bead row line 7967.
- Duel: `planning/duel/WIZARD_IDEAS_COD.md:208–286` (COD-03).
- Evidence: E692, E698.
- Code: `crates/fmine-claim/src/lib.rs:267–430`, `crates/fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs:18`.

Type and priority rationale: priority: 3 (no M0–M2 consumer; the asks feed M3–M5 consumers, each with an FM-side fallback)

## Background and why it matters
frankensim is **lift-only** for FrankenMining (FM): files are copied with provenance headers, and there is no Cargo dependency before GATE-FSIM-RECONV (§27.1). When FM needs something frankensim lacks, Appendix F.2 records an **upstream ask**: the gap, a priority, FM's interim posture and the switch-over rule. frankensim's maintainers decide whether to act; FM never edits frankensim. The six asks FD-FSIM-01…06 (plan lines 8748–8753) date from the R1 survey (E001–E010). A review of frankensim at `20463525d`, the commit pinned by §13.9 and `franken-stack.lock`, found new gaps and stale wording. A stale list leads FM consumers to plan against capabilities that are absent, or to ask the wrong crate.

## Goal
Re-verify every frankensim ask, add new ones, and record the gaps FM deliberately does not ask for, with one citation per claim at a commit, a priority and an FM fallback per row.

## Current state
- **What was read (FACT).** `~/projects/frankensim` HEAD is `20463525d9775a18c1b237d2676f364f367175ab` (2026-10-26). The working tree is dirty (`fs-matdb`, `fs-solid` and others), so every line number here comes from `git show 20463525d:<path>`.
- **FD-FSIM-01 is stale (FACT).**
  - It says "v7 pack schema", but E824 shows v1–v8 (`fs-matdb/src/pack.rs:20-34`), and §13.10 (line 1973) already says v8: the plan contradicts itself.

- **FD-FSIM-02 asks the wrong crate (FACT).** Constitutive laws are fs-material `SmallStrainLaw` implementations: two elastic laws and three J2 variants (`fs-material/src/plastic.rs:130`, `plastic/source.rs:224`, `plastic/thermal/expansion.rs:37`). `fs-solid/src/plastic3.rs:1-8` is a 3-D P1-tetrahedron driver that is generic over any law (`c1fefe8cb`, 2026-10-07). Its no-claim block (`:34-41`) states two limits:
  - P1 tetrahedra lock in confined plastic flow and over-predict limit loads, with no mixed or B-bar element;
  - there is no limit-load continuation.

  INFERENCE: shear-strength-reduction FEM (§14.2, line 2092) needs both, or its factor of safety is unconservative.

## Scope
**In:**
- the frankensim rows of F.2, plus a new sub-table F.2.1;

`id | gap | evidence (commit:path:lines) | FM consumer | priority + reason | fallback | send?`

title: NEW [WP-01]: `QuadTemporalStamp` fields to plan §6.3: physical valid time, collection time, availability time, record time
description:
## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- plan-deps: none (the done-when of closed BD-309)   proposed-deps: none
- blocks: BD-344 (no-hindsight guard), BD-336 (site metallurgical import stamps)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 2 (as-of correctness at M1–M2 depends on it; no private data or hindcasts exist yet)

## Background and why it matters
No-hindsight claims (INV-016: built `as_of_decision(t)`) need four times per observation (plan §6.3): when the physical fact held (`physical_valid_time`), when the sample or reading was collected (`collection_time`), when it became available to the decision maker (`availability_time`, e.g. an assay returned days after the sample), and when it was recorded in the system (`record_time`). A hindcast that uses an assay before its availability time is a hindsight leak.

FACT (HEAD 748da79): `QuadTemporalStamp` (`crates/fmine-time/src/lib.rs:281–291`) has `valid_time`, `transaction_time`, `decision_time_ns` and `assay_available_ns`. There is no `collection_time`, availability exists only for assays, and `decision_time` is a property of a query, not of an observation. BD-309 is closed (test `test_quad_temporal_assay_lag_guard_g_time_2`); BD-323's verdict sheet keeps it closed, which this finding contradicts.

## Goal
`QuadTemporalStamp { physical_valid_time, collection_time, availability_time, record_time }` per §6.3, with constructors that refuse impossible orders (availability before collection; record before collection), and an `as_of(t)` predicate `availability_time ≤ t ∧ record_time ≤ t`. The decision time moves to the query.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The four fields exist with the plan's names; the G-TIME-2 assay-lag test passes against them.
2. Impossible orders refuse with a typed error (never reorder or clamp).
3. All call sites migrate in the same commit; `fmine-time`'s CONTRACT.md states the semantics.
4. BD-323's verdict sheet is amended: BD-309 moves from "keep closed" to "partial", re-closed on this bead's evidence.

## Tests
Unit tests per field and per refusal; a property test that `as_of(t)` is monotone in t; the existing G-TIME-2 known answer.

## References
Plan §6.3, INV-016; `crates/fmine-time/src/lib.rs:281–291`; BD-309, BD-344, BD-336 rows; BD-344 dossier "Current state".

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read `crates/fmine-time/src/lib.rs:281-291`: `QuadTemporalStamp` has `valid_time`, `transaction_time`, `decision_time_ns`, `assay_available_ns`.
2. Plan §6.3 and bead bd-309 specify `physical_valid_time`, `collection_time`, `availability_time`, `record_time`.
3. Try to express "a grade-control sample collected on day 1, assayed and available on day 4, recorded on day 5" for a non-assay reading: there is no `collection_time`, and availability exists only for assays.

## E2E test script and logging
- **E2E (library-level).** The existing G-TIME-2 known answer, extended: a Claim whose availability time is after the as-of instant must be invisible to `as_of(t)`, and visible from that instant on.
- **Logging.** The property test logs the seed and the four timestamps of any failing stamp.

title: BD-350 [WP-15]: Target disclosure checks: remainder-grade arithmetic on drill releases, true-width and cut-off flags; one developer cash-flow replay with discounting-convention discovery
description:
_Plan row BD-350 (WP-15). Scope in one line: Target disclosure checks: drill-release arithmetic, resource-statement checks, one developer cash-flow replay_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-340
- plan-deps: BD-340   proposed-deps: BD-340, BD-127 (synthetic juniors), plus a numerics fix in which IRR refuses on non-convergence (new subtask or bead, see below)
- blocks: none (it feeds BD-229's `CapitalCandidate` rows later, as a soft link)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 3 (episodic BD and M&A use; M1–M2 by K.5; no gate depends on it)

## Background and why it matters
Before a stake, an earn-in or a bid, BD and M&A teams read a junior's or developer's own disclosures:
- drill releases ("L m @ g including l m @ g_i");
- a resource statement;
- for developers, a technical report with an economic analysis.

The plan values junior stakes on "the junior's public NI 43-101/JORC resource, haircut" (§23.2), and GB-31 shows a junior's price implying 93% conversion of inferred ounces. But nothing in the plan checks what goes into those inputs.

The duel's CC-10 (Target Disclosure Auditor; rival scores 760 and 785; K.5 row 13) proposes exact checks that are cheap and testable. Barrick's own Americas technical reports omit the economic analysis under the producing-issuer exemption (C4 §5), so a cash-flow replay belongs on developer targets, not on the issuer.

## Goal
A TargetCard computed from public documents only. It has three parts:
1. remainder-grade arithmetic and disclosure flags on drill releases;
2. resource-statement identities and cut-off reproduction;
3. one developer NPV replay with the discounting convention discovered.

Every verdict is "reproduces" or "does not reproduce under the stated inputs", never "the issuer is wrong".

## Current state (FACT)
- No Lodestar crates exist (`fmine-explore`, `fmine-prospect`), and no `fmine-econ`; that last crate is planned at layer K1 (`registries/loc_budget.toml:208`). BD-340, the exact solver, exists only in plan text.
- `ExactQty` (`crates/fmine-units/src/lib.rs:275`) supports exact mul/div and statutory conversions (oz t/st ↔ g/t is 240/7). It has no add, sub or ordering. `Money` (i128 in 10⁻⁴ units) has checked add and sub.
- **Defect.** `brent_root` (`crates/fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs:70–149`) returns `Some(b)` after `max_iter` iterations even when it has not converged (line 148). Any IRR built on it could publish a non-root. This must be fixed before any IRR is emitted (CC-10 flagged it; still present at HEAD 748da79).
- There is no intercept grammar and no release corpus. This is an M1–M2 design with no code yet.

## Scope
**In:**
- the intercept grammar and cited-mode entry;
- remainder grades on rounding intervals;
- the flags;
- resource identities through BD-340;
- the cut-off fixed point;
- NPV and payback replay with convention discovery;
- IRR with refusal;
- synthetic juniors with seeded selective reporting.

**Out:**
- re-pricing at the buyer's deck (left to BD-229 and §23.5);
- after-tax replay when no tax schedule is given (refuse);
- classification of any kind;
- embargoed data.

## Design (DESIGN)
- **Remainder grade.** For non-overlapping inclusions, g_r = (L·g − Σ lᵢ·gᵢ) / (L − Σ lᵢ). Nested inclusions form a tree evaluated bottom-up.
  - Inputs are printed decimals, so every term is an interval; BD-340 evaluates the expression exactly on intervals.
  - Units pass through `ExactQty` (feet → metres; oz/st → g/t).
- **Flags:**
  - the remainder is below the stated composite cut-off, so the headline is carried by the inclusion;
  - an inclusion's grade is below its host's;
  - downhole length is given with no true-width statement;
  - the cut-off, internal dilution or top cut is unstated;
  - a metal-equivalent grade has unstated prices or recoveries;
  - the hole sequence has gaps when a release says "results from n holes". This one is a HYPOTHESIS signal, scored against later full releases.
- **Worked example (INFERENCE on E656's printed values).** Fourmile FM24-209D is printed as "1.6 m @ 30.6 g/t within 16.3 m @ 47.07 g/t".
  - Remainder = (16.3 × 47.07 − 1.6 × 30.6) / 14.7 = 718.281 / 14.7 = **48.86 g/t**.
  - The sub-interval is lower-grade than its host. That is unusual but not an error; the card flags "inclusion below host" and asks for a re-read of deck p.6 and p.8.
- **Resource checks.** BD-340 checks tonnes × grade = metal and the category sums on rounding intervals.
  - The cut-off is reproduced as the fixed point g = cost / (net price · R(g)). Known answer E182: TRUG's 5.66 g/t reproduces at g = 5.665, R = 79.6%.
  - The "reasonable prospects" price is compared with a registered deck (E143 gives Barrick's reserve prices by year).
- **Cash-flow replay.**
  - Build NPV from the annual table in exact `Money`.
  - Discover the convention by testing a declared, finite set:
    - end-year;
    - mid-year for all flows;
    - year-0 capital undiscounted with mid-year operations.
  - A convention matches if its NPV lies inside the printed value's rounding interval. One match names the convention; zero or several refuse with "convention not discovered".
- **Synthetic worked example (labelled).** Flows are −100, 30, 40, 50, 20 ($M) at r = 5%. Under the three conventions:
  - end-year: NPV = 24.50;
  - mid-year for all flows: 25.10;
  - year-0 capital with mid-year operations: 27.57.

  A published "25.1" therefore identifies mid-year-all.
- **IRR.** A bracketed root that returns `Refused` on sign failure or non-convergence, never a last iterate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Synthetic juniors (generated drill programs rendered into release text) with seeded selective reporting have their seeds caught, and the detection rate is reported. Clean releases raise zero flags.
- One public developer replay reproduces its NPV to rounding, with the convention named. The report is chosen in week 1 as a data gate.
- E182 reproduces. The E656 arithmetic above reproduces exactly.
- No IRR is emitted from a non-converged root.

## Tests
- **Unit:**
  - remainder identity L·g = Σ lᵢgᵢ + (L − Σlᵢ)·g_r, checked exactly;
  - unit conversions;
  - each flag on minimal fixtures.
- **Property and metamorphic:**
  - reordering intervals and changing units leave the verdicts unchanged;
  - scaling all flows by k scales NPV by k and leaves the convention unchanged.
- **Known answers:** E182, E656, the synthetic NPV triple.
- **Negative and mutation:**
  - a pathological IRR case (two sign changes, no root in the bracket) refuses;
  - the old `brent_root` behaviour must fail this test;
  - after-tax with no tax schedule refuses.
- **e2e:** `fmine screen target --docs …` over a synthetic junior pack. Structured logs per interval, flag and convention test.

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **Irregular release formats.** Use cited mode: a person enters the intervals and the arithmetic still runs (K.5).
- **Episodic use.** The code is cheap to keep and also serves earn-in decisions.
- **Boundaries.**
  - Public documents only.
  - Never classify a resource or reserve (INV-002).
  - Never call a target's disclosure false.
  - Never imply any affiliation with the target or with Barrick.

## Subtasks
1. **IRR refuses on non-convergence.** Fix `brent_root`, or add a refusing wrapper, with a regression test. No sibling deps. This is a correctness defect usable on its own; consider making it its own bead now.
2. **Drill-release arithmetic and flags.** Covers the grammar, cited mode, intervals and flags. Depends on BD-340.
3. **Resource checks.** Depends on BD-340.
4. **Cash-flow replay and convention discovery.** Depends on 1.
5. **Synthetic juniors.** Seeded selective reporting rendered to text. Depends on BD-127 and 2.

## References
- Plan: §23.2 (line 4975), GB-31 (5310), K.5 row 13, bead row line 8275.
- Duel: `planning/duel/WIZARD_IDEAS_CC.md:1222–1341` (CC-10).
- Evidence: E656 (`planning/mor/MOR_CASE.md:279`), E182 (`planning/corpus/C2_nevada_technical_reports.md:411`), E143 (`C1_barrick_public_stats.md:780`).
- Code: `crates/fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs:70–149`, `crates/fmine-units/src/lib.rs:262–360`.
acceptance_criteria:
Plan done-when (§39 row BD-350): Synthetic juniors with seeded selective reporting caught; one public replay reproduces its NPV

- Synthetic juniors (generated drill programs rendered into release text) with seeded selective reporting have their seeds caught, and the detection rate is reported. Clean releases raise zero flags.
- One public developer replay reproduces its NPV to rounding, with the convention named. The report is chosen in week 1 as a data gate.
- E182 reproduces. The E656 arithmetic above reproduces exactly.
- No IRR is emitted from a non-converged root.

## Context
Subtask S2 of BD-350: "BD-350 [WP-15]: Target disclosure checks: remainder-grade arithmetic on drill releases, true-width and cut-off flags; one developer cash-flow replay with discounting-convention discovery". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** A TargetCard computed from public documents only. It has three parts:

2. resource-statement identities and cut-off reproduction;
3. one developer NPV replay with the discounting convention discovered.

Every verdict is "reproduces" or "does not reproduce under the stated inputs", never "the issuer is wrong".

## Work
REVIEW: the dossier gives no crate placement. Proposed: the kernel in `fmine-explore` (K1, Lodestar, `registries/loc_budget.toml:217`; not yet in the workspace, so an owner checkpoint needing a first slice and `CONTRACT.md`); the grammar in fmine-io (V), beside BD-345 S1's tokenizer.

- "from X m to Y m";
- ft and oz/ton (oz/st);
- hole ids such as `FM24-209D`.

Each phrase becomes `Intercept{hole, from, to, length: Printed, grade: Printed, unit, relation: Including|Within, children: Vec<Intercept>}`. "A within B" makes A a child of B. `Printed` carries the value and the step taken from its digits.

**Cited mode.** When the grammar fails, a person enters NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions rows; the arithmetic is unchanged (K.5 fallback).

**Kernel.** `fn remainder_grade(host: &Intercept) -> Result<RatInterval, Refusal>`:
- g_r = (L·g − Σ lᵢ·gᵢ)/(L − Σ lᵢ), for non-overlapping inclusions.
- Nested inclusions form a tree, evaluated bottom-up.
- Every term is an interval [v − step/2, v + step/2], evaluated exactly with BD-340 `Rat`. The expression is linear-fractional on the box, so its range is found at vertices. That only holds if L − Σ lᵢ stays strictly positive over the whole box; otherwise the kernel refuses.
- It also refuses overlapping inclusions.

**Units through exact factors:**
- ft → m is 3048/10000. Add this constant to fmine-units, beside the existing ones.
- oz/st → g/t is 240/7 (`OZ_PER_ST_TO_G_PER_T_NUM`/`_DEN`, `crates/fmine-units/src/lib.rs`).
- `ExactQty` has no add or sub (`:275`), so this subtask needs BD-340's `Rat` operations.

**Flags (from the dossier):**
- the remainder is below the stated composite cut-off (the headline is carried by the inclusion);
- an inclusion's grade is below its host's;
- a downhole length is given with no true-width statement;
- the cut-off, internal dilution or top cut is unstated;
- a metal-equivalent grade has unstated prices or recoveries;
- the hole sequence has gaps under "results from n holes" (HYPOTHESIS, scored later in S5).

**Known answer: E656, an arithmetic check only.** FM24-209D prints "1.6 m @ 30.6 g/t within 16.3 m @ 47.07 g/t".
- Remainder = (16.3 × 47.07 − 1.6 × 30.6)/14.7 = 718.281/14.7 = 48.86 g/t. Exactly, that is 718281/14700.
- The card flags "inclusion below host" and asks for a re-read of deck p.6 and p.8.
- Fourmile itself is a walled lane under the plan (§37.3, E139), so no TargetCard is issued about Fourmile.

**Wording.** "Reproduces" or "does not reproduce under the stated inputs".

**Builds on:** BD-340 S1.
**Hands over:** the grammar and flags to S5, and the TargetCard section to the verb.

**Never:** classify a resource (INV-002); call a disclosure false; use embargoed data; imply affiliation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- E656 reproduces exactly: the interval encloses 718281/14700 (48.86 g/t), and "inclusion below host" fires.
- The remainder identity holds exactly.
- Each flag fires on its minimal fixture, and clean fixtures raise none.
- Unit conversions are exact.
- Reordering intervals or changing units leaves the verdicts unchanged.

## Tests and logging

title: BD-350.S3 [WP-15]: Resource checks
description:
## Context
Subtask S3 of BD-350: "BD-350 [WP-15]: Target disclosure checks: remainder-grade arithmetic on drill releases, true-width and cut-off flags; one developer cash-flow replay with discounting-convention discovery". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** A TargetCard computed from public documents only. It has three parts:
1. remainder-grade arithmetic and disclosure flags on drill releases;
2. resource-statement identities and cut-off reproduction;
3. one developer NPV replay with the discounting convention discovered.

Every verdict is "reproduces" or "does not reproduce under the stated inputs", never "the issuer is wrong".

## Work
REVIEW: `fmine_metrics::solve_cutoff_grade` (`crates/fmine-metrics/src/lib.rs:176`) already claims E182–E184 (BD-275), but it has three defects:
- it clamps recovery to [0.05, 0.999] (line 188);
- it floors the price at 1e-9 (line 186);
- it returns the last iterate after 100 iterations without converging (line 195).

That is the same defect class as `brent_root`. Its only test (line 269) uses synthetic inputs, not E182. This subtask should retire it, or replace it with the refusing solver below, in the same commit or under NEW-irr-refuses.

**Goal.** Resource-statement checks and cut-off reproduction for target disclosures. Placement is OPEN, as in S2:
- the identity binding goes in fmine-public (V), on BD-340;
- the cut-off solver goes in the chosen K-layer crate.

**Resource identities.** These go through BD-340 on rounding intervals:
- **Metal.** Tonnes × grade = metal: `Ratio{rate: grade, num: metal, den: tonnes, k}` with the exact factor 31.1034768 g per troy ounce (`TROY_OZ_TO_GRAMS_NUM`/`_DEN`).
- **Category sums.** Measured + Indicated = M&I, and the other sums printed in the statement.
- **Outcomes.** Feasible means reproduces; Infeasible carries a certificate and BD-340 S3 blame. Units never convert implicitly.

**Cut-off fixed point.** g = cost/(net price · R(g)). The function is `fn cutoff_fixed_point(cost, net_per_g, recovery: RecoveryCard, bracket) -> Result<Rat or Root, Refusal>`.

**Known answer: E182.** TRUG resource COG 5.66 g/t (T p.168 Table 14-5; C2 §4).
- Inputs: total cost $243.89/t; gold $1,700/oz; AB495 1.02%; refining $0.38/oz; R(g) = 100.79 − 155.7·0.771/g, in percent.
- Result: g = 5.665 and R = 79.6%.
- For this recovery form, g·R(g) is affine in g, so the fixed point has an exact closed form (INFERENCE, arithmetic):
  - g = (100·cost/net + 155.7·0.771)/100.79;
  - net = (1,700·(1 − 0.0102) − 0.38)/31.1034768 $/g.
- A general R(g) uses NEW-irr-refuses' bracketed root finder. NotConverged, NoSignChange or NonFinite become a refusal, never a number.
- A recovery outside [0, 100]% refuses. It is never clamped.

**Reasonable-prospects price.** Compare the statement's price with a registered deck, and report which deck it matches. This is never a verdict on the target.
- E143 gives Barrick's reserve prices by year: gold $1,200 (2020–21), $1,300 (2022–23), $1,400 (2024), $1,500 (2025); copper $2.75, $3.00, $3.00 and $3.25.
- `PriceDeck::barrick_reserve` (`crates/fmine-metrics/src/lib.rs:92`) covers only 2023–2025 (E606). A comparison for another year cites E143 directly.

**Builds on:** BD-340 S1–S2, and NEW-irr-refuses for general recovery cards.
**Hands over:** the resource section of the TargetCard.

**Never:**
- classify a resource or reserve (INV-002);
- call a statement false;
- clamp;
- reuse `solve_cutoff_grade` as it stands.

## Acceptance Criteria
- E182 reproduces: g = 5.665 to three decimals and R = 79.6%. The closed form and the root-finder path agree.
- A non-converging or non-finite cut-off solve refuses. No clamped recovery is ever used.
- Synthetic resource statements: consistent ones are Feasible; a seeded category-sum or tonnes × grade conflict is Infeasible, with a checked certificate.
- The deck comparison names the registered deck and its E id.

## Tests and logging
**Known answers:**
- `test_e182_trug_cutoff_fixed_point_5_665`.
- `test_e182_closed_form_equals_root_finder`.

**Refusals:**
- `test_cutoff_refuses_on_nonconvergence`.
- `test_cutoff_refuses_recovery_outside_unit_interval`.
- `test_old_solve_cutoff_grade_clamp_regression`: pinned to the 2026-10-29 defect. The old function returns a number on an input where the new solver refuses.

**Identities:**
- `test_tonnes_grade_metal_identity_on_intervals` (synthetic).
- `test_category_sum_conflict_certificate` (synthetic).

**Deck:**
- `test_reasonable_prospects_price_vs_registered_deck` (E143).

**Metamorphic:**
- `test_unit_change_g_per_t_vs_oz_per_st_invariant` (240/7).

**E2E log lines:**
- Per identity: `{"event":"resource_check","identity","cells","outcome","certificate_digest"}`.

- Summary: `{"event":"resource_summary","identities","feasible","infeasible","refused"}`.

title: BD-350.S4 [WP-15]: Cash-flow replay and convention discovery
description:
## Context
Subtask S4 of BD-350: "BD-350 [WP-15]: Target disclosure checks: remainder-grade arithmetic on drill releases, true-width and cut-off flags; one developer cash-flow replay with discounting-convention discovery". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** A TargetCard computed from public documents only. It has three parts:
1. remainder-grade arithmetic and disclosure flags on drill releases;
2. resource-statement identities and cut-off reproduction;
3. one developer NPV replay with the discounting convention discovered.

Every verdict is "reproduces" or "does not reproduce under the stated inputs", never "the issuer is wrong".

## Work
REVIEW: "Build NPV in exact `Money`" cannot hold for the mid-year conventions, because (1 + r)^(−½) is irrational. Compute that factor as a rational enclosure: bisection on squares, with no transcendentals (NEW-det-portable-kernels). Then test a match by interval logic: a straddle refines up to a cap, and if it is still undecided the convention refuses. The owner should confirm.

**Depends on NEW-irr-refuses.** That bug bead changes `brent_root` (`crates/fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs:70`, which returns `Some(b)` unconditionally at line 148) to return `Result<Root, RootError>`. This subtask also builds on BD-340's intervals.

**Placement.** `fmine-econ` (K1, Helm; charter "NPV with exact money"; `registries/loc_budget.toml:208`). It is not in the workspace yet, so adding it is an owner checkpoint: it needs a first real slice and a `CONTRACT.md`.

**Inputs.** Each is a cited NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions row:
- the annual cash-flow table, in $M at the printed step;
- the discount rate;
- the printed NPV and its step;
- the printed IRR (optional);
- the tax schedule (optional).

**NPV.**
- Sum in `Money` (`crates/fmine-units/src/lib.rs:423`; `checked_add` and `checked_sub` at `:456`/`:470`).
- Integer-power factors (1 + r)^(−t) are exact rationals.
- The ½-power factor is the enclosure [lo, hi] with lo² ≤ 1 + r ≤ hi².
- Flow rounding intervals propagate, so the NPV is an interval.

**Convention discovery.** The declared set is:
- `EndYear`;
- `MidYearAll`;
- `Year0UndiscountedMidYearOps`.

A convention matches if its NPV interval meets the printed rounding interval. One match names the convention. Zero matches, or several, refuse with "convention not discovered". FMINE-REF-104 (non-identifiable) is the plan meaning; the code is finalised with BD-328.

**Synthetic known answer (labelled).** Flows −100, 30, 40, 50 and 20 ($M) at r = 5% give:
- end-year: 24.50;
- mid-year for all flows: 25.10;
- year-0 capital undiscounted with mid-year operations: 27.57.

A printed "25.1" ([25.05, 25.15]) therefore identifies mid-year-all only.

**IRR.**
- It is a bracketed root of NPV(r) under the discovered convention, found with the refusing root finder.
- It refuses on no sign change, non-convergence or a non-finite value.
- Cash flows with more than one sign change may have several roots. Refuse, or report every bracketed root; never pick one.
- Synthetic example (labelled, arithmetic): −100, +230, −132 has roots at 10% and 20%. The bracket [0.30, 0.50] has no sign change.

**After-tax replay** with no tax schedule refuses.

**Week-1 data gate.** Choose one public developer technical report with an economic analysis. Register it (URL, sha256, `published_at`, pages) and record the choice. Producer reports often omit the analysis (C4 §5).

**Never:**
- emit an IRR from a non-converged root;
- pick a convention per flow;
- call the printed NPV wrong;
- imply affiliation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The synthetic triple reproduces to 2 dp: 24.50, 25.10 and 27.57. "25.1" names mid-year-all.
- Zero or several matches refuse with "convention not discovered".
- One public developer replay reproduces its NPV to rounding, with the convention named and every input cited.
- No IRR is emitted from a non-converged root. Under the old `brent_root` behaviour the pathological case fails.
- An after-tax replay without a tax schedule refuses.

## Tests and logging
**Known answers:**
- `test_npv_end_year_24_50`.
- `test_npv_mid_year_all_25_10`.
- `test_npv_year0_undiscounted_27_57`.
- `test_printed_25_1_identifies_mid_year_all`.

**Refusals:**
- `test_convention_not_discovered_zero_or_several`.
- `test_irr_refuses_no_sign_change_bracket`.
- `test_irr_two_sign_changes_never_picks_one`.
- `test_irr_refuses_not_converged`.
- `test_after_tax_without_schedule_refuses`.

**Properties:**
- `test_scaling_flows_by_k_scales_npv_keeps_convention`.
- `test_mid_year_factor_enclosure_contains_root`.

**Ignored real-file test.** `test_developer_npv_replay_public_report` runs in BD-339's CI job.
- Per convention: `{"event":"npv_convention","convention","npv_lo","npv_hi","printed","printed_step","match"}`.
- Summary: `{"event":"npv_replay","report","sha256","convention","irr_state"}`.

## Close rule
Close only with this subtask's own evidence, as typed references: `test:<crate>::<path>::<fn>`, `commit:<sha7>`, `record:<path>`, `ci:<run-id>@<sha7>` or an E id. Never a shared or generic reason (K.2 finding 4).

- The synthetic triple reproduces to 2 dp: 24.50, 25.10 and 27.57. "25.1" names mid-year-all.
- Zero or several matches refuse with "convention not discovered".
- One public developer replay reproduces its NPV to rounding, with the convention named and every input cited.
- No IRR is emitted from a non-converged root. Under the old `brent_root` behaviour the pathological case fails.
- An after-tax replay without a tax schedule refuses.

title: BD-350.S5 [WP-15]: Synthetic juniors
description:
## Context
Subtask S5 of BD-350: "BD-350 [WP-15]: Target disclosure checks: remainder-grade arithmetic on drill releases, true-width and cut-off flags; one developer cash-flow replay with discounting-convention discovery". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** A TargetCard computed from public documents only. It has three parts:
1. remainder-grade arithmetic and disclosure flags on drill releases;
2. resource-statement identities and cut-off reproduction;
3. one developer NPV replay with the discounting convention discovered.

Every verdict is "reproduces" or "does not reproduce under the stated inputs", never "the issuer is wrong".

## Work
REVIEW: no subtask owns the parent's verb, `fmine screen target --docs …`, or its `verbs.toml` row. Proposal: S5 carries it, because its end-to-end run over a synthetic junior pack is the verb's first full use.

**Goal.** Synthetic juniors: generated drill programs rendered into release text, with seeded selective reporting.

**Depends on:**
- BD-127 (the `fmine-gen` framework with sealed truth; open; layer T; `registries/loc_budget.toml:514`);
- S2 (grammar, remainder kernel and flags).

**Files:**
- New module `crates/fmine-gen/src/junior.rs`, inside BD-127's crate.
- The verb in `crates/fmine-cli/src/lib.rs` (`CliCommand::ScreenTarget{docs}`), registered in `registries/verbs.toml` (`path = "screen target"`, `subsystem = "Lodestar"`) and in the robot-docs list (line 284).

**Layering.** fmine-cli is layer U and cannot depend on fmine-gen, layer T (`registries/workspace_topology.toml`). So the generator writes the pack as text files under `target/synthetic_juniors/`, and the CLI reads them as documents. No reverse dependency is needed.

**Generator (DESIGN).** `JuniorWorld{seed: RngKey, holes, composites, grade_process, cutoff, reporting: Reporting}`. It renders releases in S2's grammar forms: "L m @ g g/t including …" and "within".

**Seeded selective-reporting classes.** Each is sealed, so the engine never sees the label:
1. a headline carried by an inclusion, with a remainder below the stated cut-off;
2. omitted holes under "results from n holes";
3. a downhole length with no true-width statement;
4. a metal-equivalent grade with unstated prices or recoveries;
5. an unstated cut-off, internal dilution or top cut;
6. clean releases, with no seed.

**Hole-gap signal (HYPOTHESIS).** It is scored against the "later full release" that the same sealed world renders.

**Scoring.** The harness opens the seal and reports detection per class with a 90% Clopper–Pearson interval. Generation is deterministic through `PhiloxStream`. Every output is labelled synthetic and is never presented as a real junior's disclosure.

**Builds on:** S2, plus S3 and S4 sections when present.
**Hands over:** the detection-rate report to the K.5 record. The TargetCard e2e feeds BD-229 later as a soft link.

**Never:**
- let the engine read seed labels;
- tune the flags on the scored replicates;
- name or resemble a real company in the synthetic text;
- put any real issuer's identity in the synthetic packs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each seeded class is caught, and its detection rate and interval are reported.
- Clean synthetic releases raise zero flags across all replicates.
- Every rendered release round-trips through S2's grammar to the generated intervals.
- `fmine screen target --docs target/synthetic_juniors/<pack>` runs end to end, writing structured logs per interval, flag and convention test.
- The verb is registered, and `cargo run -p xtask -- check-all` passes.

- `test_each_seed_class_detected_with_rate`.
- `test_hole_gap_hypothesis_scored_against_full_release`.

- `test_generator_deterministic_under_rng_key`.

**Negative controls:**
- `test_engine_input_has_no_seed_labels`: sealed-truth type check.
- `test_cli_screen_target_usage_errors`.

**E2E.** `test_cli_screen_target_synthetic_pack` runs in the normal lane; no corpus is needed.

- Per flag: `{"event":"flag","doc","kind","seeded","detected"}`.

title: NEW [WP-03]: Commit the independent oracle readers behind E820–E823 under `scripts/oracle/`, so GATE-BULL-01's reference read is reproducible from the repository
description:
## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)

## Background and why it matters
GATE-BULL-01 part 1 (extraction fidelity) is measured "against a reference read independent of the importer" (plan §21.6). AGENTS.md: "Never regenerate an oracle fixture from the candidate." For the M0 run of 2026-10-29, an independent Python reader and census were written FIRST, their outputs pinned, and only then was the Rust code written against them (MOR_CASE, paragraph before E820). E820 (extraction fidelity: 101 visible and 6 hidden sheets, 30,388 numeric cells, 3,952 placeholders, 1,092 formula errors, 6,537 text cells, per-file numeric digests), E822 (ledger: 34 tables, 519 subject columns, 2,595 instances; i 2,120, ii 3, iii 4, iv 17, v 391, np 60) and E823 rest on them.

FACT (2026-10-29): those scripts are not in the repository. They exist only in the session scratch directory `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jemanuel-projects-franken-mining/2ba72fbb-c45d-4fd8-93cf-c08cb26d7a18/scratchpad/`:

- `scripts/rate_census.py`: the per-ounce rate census.
A `/tmp` directory can be cleaned at any time. Until the scripts are committed, nobody else can reproduce the evidence the M0 gate rests on.

## Tests
A CI-free smoke run is enough: the ignored real-file Rust test and these scripts are run together by BD-339's CI job once the kit exists. Log one JSON line per file (`file`, `sha256`, `numeric`, `placeholders`, `formula_errors`, `text`, `digest`) and a summary line.

The scripts were written for one session; they may hard-code paths. Parameterise paths only.

## References

description:
_Plan row BD-322 (WP-03). Scope in one line: Source registry pinning the real workbooks, and the label-anchored importer rebuilt on it (K.2 step 3)_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-321, BD-271
- plan-deps: BD-321, BD-271   proposed-deps: BD-321 (closed); child "Label-anchored Mine Stats reader" (open). BD-271 is closed under the generic reason, but its Mine Stats promise is unmet; the child bead carries that work.
- blocks: BD-065 (K.6 edge: the reproduction harness runs on registered inputs only), BD-329, BD-332, BD-338, BD-339

Type and priority rationale: priority: 0 (K.2 pre-push step 3 and GATE-BULL-01's input contract; registry and AISC half DONE in 543df53; Mine Stats half open as a child bead)

## Background and why it matters
Round 7 (Appendix K.2 finding 3; R7-C007–R7-C010, R7-C063) found that the M0 parser works. It read all 18 real Barrick workbooks and matched an independent reader exactly. What failed were three things:
- the compiled-in file list;
- the hard-coded sheet name ("Gold AISC");
- fixed cell coordinates.

Real workbooks drift every quarter. Rows are inserted (a "Revenue" row appeared in Q2 2026), regions are re-mapped (Pueblo Viejo moved from South America to North America in Q4 2025), and labels change footnote digits. An importer on fixed coordinates silently reads the wrong cell.

B7 (the assurance-chain pass, Appendix K.4 rule 1) adds a further requirement. Each imported value must be bound to its bytes *and* its interpretation: the cell, header, unit, basis, subject and publication vintage, with the raw token kept. An anchor alone proves too little.

**The plan's done-when has two parts:**
1. "All 18 registered files import by label".
2. "The run's input manifest equals the registry".

## What exists (FACT, commit 543df53)
**The registry.** `crates/fmine-public/src/sources.rs`:
- `RegisteredSource{file_name, kind, quarter, url, url_basis, bytes, sha256_hex}` for 18 files. These are Mine Stats Q1 2024–Q2 2026 (10 files) and the AISC reconciliation workbooks Q3 2024–Q2 2026 (8 files), downloaded from Barrick's public CDN on 2026-10-29 03:35:00Z–03:36:24Z.
- `IssuerProfile` (`BARRICK`), with `corpus_dir` `corpus_of_input_docs/downloaded/mine_stats`, the subjects (18 site and region names), and the registered reconstructions (three E816 entries, each re-verified by label checks).
- `issuer_profile("barrick")`.

**Loading.**
- `load_registered_sources` verifies the byte length and sha256 of each file before reading it.
- A mismatch refuses with FMINE-REF-502, naming both digests (test `fmine-public/tests/registry.rs`).

**AISC tables, label-anchored.** `crates/fmine-public/src/aisc.rs` `locate_table`:
- finds the cost-of-sales, TCC, AISC, ounces and per-ounce rows by their labels;
- finds the header row as the row with the most subject matches;
- matches subjects exactly, or with one footnote letter.

The real run reads 34 visible AISC tables and 2,595 identity instances. It equals an independent Python reader (E820–E822).

**Census.** Every one of the 18 files gets a cell census and a numeric digest (`Workbook::cell_census`). Those equal the independent reader for all 18.

## What is NOT done (why this bead stays open)
**The Mine Stats workbooks (10 of 18) are not imported by label.** They are loaded, digest-checked and censused, but no table is located or read from them. That work is the child bead "Label-anchored Mine Stats reader". It is also the unmet half of closed BD-271, whose done-when promised:
- "the 3,996 parsed cells of the Q1/Q2 2026 Mine Stats reproduce exactly";
- "the 7 zero placeholders import as Nil";
- "all ten W1 workbooks import under the versioned region map";
- "the Q3 2026 file imports on release day without code changes".

**No explicit test asserts that the run's input manifest equals the registry.** It holds by construction (the loader iterates the registry), but done-when part 2 needs a test. The test must compare the report's `sources` array (file, sha256, bytes) with `BARRICK.sources`, element by element.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Child "Label-anchored Mine Stats reader" is closed.
2. A test asserts that the report's input manifest equals the registry: the same 18 files, in registry order, with equal sha256 and byte counts. It runs in the default suite on the synthetic lane's registry, and in the ignored real-file test on the real lane.
3. The real-file test asserts that all 18 files contributed located tables: 8 AISC files through `locate_table`, and 10 Mine Stats files through the new reader.

## Tests
- Unit: manifest equals registry, on the synthetic profile.
- E2E (ignored, real corpus; runs in BD-339's CI job): manifest equality plus per-file table counts. Log one structured line per file: `file`, `kind`, `sha256`, `tables_located`, `cells_read`, `refusals`.

## Risks and notes
- **The registry is compiled in.** Registering the Q3 2026 release (due 2026-11-09) needs a code change today. The bead "Quarterly vintage ingestion" moves the registry to `registries/sources/barrick.toml`. That is its job; this bead does not block on it.
- **Never commit workbook bytes.** `corpus_of_input_docs/` is gitignored. Whether derived values may be committed is OPEN-R7-1.

## References
Plan Appendix K.2 (finding 3, step 3), K.4 rule 1; §21.6; BD-271 row; MOR_CASE E820–E823; W1 (`planning/research/W1_barrick_mine_stats.md`) §3 and §13.
